The coaching staffs range from Terrell Williams and Todd Downing to Mike Kafka and Dan Skipper. But the ties between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions do not end on the sidelines or in the booth.

Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, eight players in the fold for the trip to Germany have been members of both locker rooms during their NFL careers.

Here's a glance through the list of ex-Patriots and ex-Lions ahead of Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at FC Bayern Munich Stadium.

Joshua Dobbs, quarterback — One March after signing, the Patriots released Dobbs with one year left on his contract. The veteran backup checked into four games during his lone season working alongside starter, captain, Pro Bowler and All-Pro Drake Maye. He completed 7-of-10 passes for 65 yards with no touchdowns nor interceptions. Entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2017 draft at No. 135 overall by way of the Tennessee Volunteers, Dobbs logged previous stops with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars, Cleveland Browns, Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals, Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers. The 31-year-old was previously in Detroit, too, and returned during training camp following the retirement of Teddy Bridgewater. The journey has brought 28 games, including 15 starts, while completing 62.8 percent of his passes for 3,346 yards with 17 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. An additional 515 yards and eight scores have been logged as a rusher.

DeAndre Carter, wide receiver — A former FCS All-American out of Sacramento State, Carter made stops with the Baltimore Ravens and Oakland Raiders before signing to head coach Bill Belichick's practice squad as an undrafted rookie in December 2015. He would be released, re-signed and retained on a futures contract at Gillette Stadium en route to catching a touchdown the following preseason. The 33-year-old has since toured double-digit teams around the league and went from the practice squad to the 53-man roster of the Lions in October. Through 114 career games, he stands with 1,336 receiving yards, 99 rushing yards and six touchdowns on offense. A seventh TD arrived on special teams, where Carter's run includes 1,523 yards on punt returns and 3,468 yards on kickoff returns.

K.J. Britt, linebacker — The Lions turned to the Patriots' practice squad to poach Britt at the start of November. The 27-year-old linebacker now resides on the 53-man roster in Detroit after making the initial cut in Foxborough only to be released as a vested veteran and called upon as a standard elevation. Signed to a one-year pact last offseason, Britt's career includes 78 games and 16 starts. Selected in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL draft at No. 176 overall, the Auburn product spent his rookie pact with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and finished atop the Miami Dolphins with 76.9 percent of the workload on special teams in 2025. He stands with 162 tackles, half a sack, four stops for loss and three passes defensed through 994 snaps on defense and 1,315 snaps on special teams.

Myles Bryant, safety — After four seasons with the Patriots, Bryant's stay reached its end in 2024 as he agreed to terms with the Houston Texans. A brief stop in the AFC North followed before the 28-year-old defensive back moved on to the NFC South as part of Detroit's practice squad in October. Originally arrived in Foxborough as an undrafted rookie out of Washington in 2020, Bryant went on to appear in 55 games for the Patriots, including 17 starts, while recording 200 tackles, two sacks, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and four interceptions. He now finds himself 77 games into his run in the league while seeing 2,514 snaps on defense and 515 snaps in the kicking game.

Cory Durden, defensive tackle — Durden has been in New England's starting lineup for all nine games this fall. The nose tackle stands with 22 tackles, the initial 1.5 sacks of his NFL career, as well as a new best with five quarterback hits. He began 2025 on the practice squad in Foxborough before quickly earning a promotion to the 53-man roster, appearing in every game on the way to Super Bowl LX. Entering the league as an undrafted free agent by way of Florida State and North Carolina State in 2023, Durden spent his rookie training camp with the Lions before being waived at the cutdown deadline. Stints with the Los Angeles Rams and New York Giants were also part of his path. The 27-year-old had checked into eight games to notch 13 tackles before becoming a Patriot.

Erick Hunter, linebacker — An undrafted rookie out of Morgan State, Hunter signed his first NFL contract with the Lions in the spring. The stay ended at the league's 53-man reduction in August. After clearing waivers, the 23-year-old made his way to the active roster of the Patriots. Now eight appearances into his stay at Gillette Stadium, Hunter has played 14 downs on defense while cutting his teeth with 132 downs on special teams. The 6-foot-4, 224-pound linebacker has stepped in as an oversized gunner downing punts and sits with 13 combined tackles, including one for loss. As far as the Patriots' kicking game goes, he currently sits tied for the team lead in stops while ranking sixth in terms of snaps played.

Carlton Davis III, cornerback — Davis' Patriots tenure has featured 22 starts in the regular season, plus 96 tackles, including four for loss, and a dozen passes defensed. The 29-year-old cornerback arrived in Foxborough on a three-year deal as an unrestricted free agent in 2025 and has been limited to five appearances this campaign due to injury. Originally entering the NFL in the second round of the 2018 class at No. 63 overall, the Auburn product earned a Super Bowl LV ring while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The run ended via trade as Davis headed to Detroit along with a pair of sixth-rounders in exchange for a third-rounder that became wide receiver Jalen McMillan. Davis started 13 contests during his lone year as a Lion, tallying 56 tackles, two interceptions, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries.

Kindle Vildor, cornerback — The 28-year-old Vildor signed with New England in March and began September on the practice squad after being released as a vested veteran. He went from serving as a standard elevation to earning a 53-man roster spot in October, yet has since returned to the 17-man group. Vildor stands with seven tackles, one stop for loss, one pass deflection and one forced fumble across a handful of appearances for the Patriots. Originally entering the league with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, the Georgia Southern product spent time with five other organizations before landing in the AFC East. Count the Lions among them from 2024 into 2025. Through 85 career games, including 27 starts, the corner has had a hand in 147 tackles, one sack, two forced fumbles and two interceptions across 2,158 snaps on defense and 605 snaps in the kicking game.

#2740. Fran Tarkenton raves about Kirk Cousins's return to Minnesota

On Monday night, I was explaining to my wife the bizarre situation in Minnesota, where a championship-caliber defense has been paired with an offense that would have trouble scoring a touchdown in the lower divisions of college football.

She said, “Is Fran Tarkenton still around?”

Actually, he is. And the end result to the expedited search came from the Tarkenton playbook: The Vikings brought back a former Vikings quarterback in trading with the Raiders for Kirk Cousins.

On Tuesday, Tarkenton gushed about the return of Cousins. “I think it’s the greatest thing that could have happened to us,” Tarkenton told Darren Wolfson of KSTP. “We were lost. We were winning on defense. We had no offense. We had no quarterback. And now we’ve got Kirk coming back, who is having a great year. He’s a great player. He’s a better person than player. Our team should lift up now. And we’re in the best division in football. Our defense has kept us in the hunt.

“And having Kirk — I cannot tell you how happy I am for the Vikings, for the fans, for the Wilfs, and for all the players and the old-timers like myself. We’ve got a chance with Kirk Cousins.”

Tarkenton spent 1961 through 1966 with the Vikings before returning from 1972 through 1978. And, as it turns out, his comments about Cousins weren’t the only news he made this week.

Tarkenton apparently earned a mere $1.2 million during his entire 18-year NFL career. But that was just the starting point. He has amassed enough of a fortune in the business world to recently buy — at age 86 — a $51.89 million home in Palm Beach.

Tarkenton blazed the trail for today’s former quarterbacks who work even harder in retirement. He was the first NFL player to host Saturday Night Live, and his TV career included a co-hosting gig on That’s Incredible and a four-year stint in the Monday Night Football booth.

The big money came in the business world, specifically computer software. He also has made many millions as an early investor in Apple.

And, if you watch the clip, you’ll see that Tarkenton still has a verbal and mental fastball.

The return of Cousins definitely conjures memories of Tarkenton’s second act in Minnesota, which resulted in three Super Bowl appearances.

The Vikings would be thrilled if, with Cousins back in the fold, they could manage just one.

#2736. John Spytek: Fernando Mendoza passed every test, allowed us to make a hard decision

It took longer than it has for most quarterbacks drafted first overall, but Fernando Mendoza’s time has come in Las Vegas.

Tuesday’s trade of Kirk Cousins means that Mendoza is now the No. 1 quarterback for the Raiders and he’ll make his first NFL start in Sunday’s game against the Seahawks. The Raiders went into the season determined to give Mendoza as much time as possible to learn from Cousins and their 4-5 start made it possible to stick with the plan rather than turn attention to the future.

The move would have waited a little while longer if the Vikings were not motivated buyers in the wake of Monday night’s disastrous performance against the Bills, but General Manager John Spytek said at a Tuesday press conference that the trade would not have happened without Mendoza showing the team that he’s ready.

“It’s something that he’s worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building,” Spytek said. “He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he’s earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback.”

While the Raiders feel Mendoza is ready, it is a big change to go from the practice field to game action and the Seahawks are a tough first opponent for the rookie. The Raiders drafted Mendoza to be their leader, however, and head coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza has “exceeded those expectations” while learning from a good teacher.

“I think with the right role model that will accelerate his growth and we had, you know, we had the right role model,” Kubiak said.

Becoming the starter is just the beginning for Mendoza and it kicks off an era the Raiders hope will bring them back to the upper rungs of the AFC in the years to come.

#2734. Füllkrug addresses age concerns after returning to Germany squad under Klopp

Topping the Bundesliga's scoring charts with nine goals for Werder Bremen, Niclas Füllkrug has been recalled to the Germany squad by Jürgen Klopp for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Serbia on Friday and the Netherlands on Monday.

A few weeks before announcing his latest squad, Klopp seemed to suggest that Füllkrug's age of 33 was a disadvantage as he looks to build a Germany team for the future.

"Niclas Füllkrug scores goal after goal in the Bundesliga, but he's 33. That's not my fault," Klopp said in an interview with DAZN last month.

"We have the present, the medium-term future and the long-term future. In the present, it can of course work; in the medium term, possibly as well. Long term, well, we'll have to see."

While Klopp has since admitted that he is "not thrilled" with the statements he made in that interview, Füllkrug himself addressed his age at a press conference on Monday.

"My age is a fact, but it's not something I think about too much. I've spoken to the head coach about it and I didn't take his comments personally in the slightest," he said.

"We're at a stage where the focus is on developing young players. We've got several players who are really making an impression at the moment, so there are plenty of options to choose from."

Overall, the West Ham loanee is simply happy to be back in the squad for the first time in over a year.

"I'm delighted to be back. It's recognition of the work you put in and how you perform for your club. It's great to be part of the national team again and to have the chance to train under Jürgen Klopp," he said.

"I've caught up with a lot of familiar faces and met plenty of new ones too. The squad looks very different now and you can really feel how much has changed. I'm happy that I can just be myself and that people respond positively to that."

#2733. Jaguars GM James Gladstone: We value draft picks, but don't always use them in April

Jaguars General Manager James Gladstone doesn’t view this week’s moves to acquire safety Jessie Bates, defensive tackle Jordan Davis, and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in the same light as many others around the football world have characterized them.

Gladstone sent away the team’s 2027 first- and second-round picks, 2028 fifth- and sixth-round picks, and 2029 second-round pick in three Monday trades, which has been positioned as going all-in on maximizing the team’s Super Bowl chances after a 6-2 start. In a Tuesday press conference, Gladstone said he wouldn’t “necessarily” use the same framing and said he’d describe the team’s approach as always “getting better as a football team and prioritizing getting better as a football team.”

Another popular response has been that Gladstone has adopted his former Rams boss Les Snead’s “F them picks” to building the team’s Super Bowl LVI winners and subsequent teams. Gladstone noted that the Rams made plenty of picks while he was there from 2017-2024 and that he always takes into account the compensatory draft pick process during free agency as a way to supplement assets that can be used in a variety of ways.

“It’s a very symbiotic process that encompasses a lot of layers to it, but it’s certainly not ‘F them picks,’” Gladstone said. “While that’s been characterized as the approach, it’s not necessarily — we actually value picks. We don’t always use them on the three days that exist in April.”

Gladstone also acknowledged that “a part of it” is acquiring known commodities rather than gambling on the unknown trajectories of draft picks. There’s a gamble involved with the Jaguars’ approach as well and the way it pays off will be a big part of Gladstone’s ultimate legacy in Jacksonville.

#2730. Commanders GM Adam Peters: Ball needs to go in the end zone on final play

The Commanders’ operation at the end of games came under the microscope again in Week 9.

Washington was down 20-13 with the ball at the Rams’ 31-yard-line with three seconds left and their final play saw quarterback Jayden Daniels hit tight end Chig Okonkwo with a short pass. Okonkwo got down around the 10 before he attempted to lateral to a teammate. The attempt at a Stanford band-esque ending fizzled out from there and the Commanders fell to 2-5-1 on the season.

The Commanders were in position to lose due to several things that went wrong over the first 59 minutes and 57 seconds of play, but they still had a chance to tie or win the game, which is one that General Manager Adam Peters said they should have taken during a Wednesday appearance on 106.7 The Fan.

“There’s a couple things on that, but I think the bottom line is the ball needs to get in the end zone there,” Peters said.

Last Sunday’s ending may not have been as egregious an error as the one Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn made at the end of their tie with the Giants, but it was enough of an error that the case for changing those in charge of the on-field operation is even stronger heading into Week 10.

#2729. Lakers vs. Bucks Preview: Trap game in the making

The streaking Lakers (10-2) continue their current four-game road trip in Milwaukee where they will take on the Bucks (1-10). This is the first matchup between the teams this season.

Who: Los Angeles Lakers vs. Milwaukee Bucks

The Lakers have been playing a lot of basketball lately.

Although the Lakers have been playing like a very good team, their schedule hasn't made it easy. They've played four games in the last seven nights and this East Coast road trip has only added to the challenge. They have a well-deserved three-day break coming up. But first, they're going to face arguably the worst team in the league.

This certainly has all the makings of a trap game.

They should be able to win given how serious they've approached every game ahead of them thus far this season. The theme of this road trip has been their next-man mentality, which has kept their winning streak to six straight games. On Wednesday, it's another chance to keep building.

Los Angeles will take on a Milwaukee team led by Tyler Herro (who is currently listed as day-to-day with an injury), Kyle Kuzma and Jaime Jaquez Jr. Basically, it's a rebuilding Bucks team that moved on to its next chapter without franchise legend Giannis Antetokounmpo. They've been experiencing some growing pains on both ends of the floor, where they rank in the bottom five in the league. While they're a very good rebounding team, the Bucks don't have the firepower to keep up with the Lakers — at least they shouldn't.

The only way this match becomes a threat for the Lakers is if one of their streaky players — like Kuzma, Jaquez Jr. or Ryan Rollins — turns out to be the best player on the floor. That's going to be extremely hard to do with Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves set to play.

Hopefully, it won't take much from Dončić and Reaves to get the Lakers through. It would be nice to see the role players and bench continue to build on the momentum they've gained.

Remember, it's games like this that end up being huge in the standings down the line. These are must-win games for the purple and gold, especially in the competitive Western Conference where they're currently sitting on top of the standings.

Let's see if the Lakers can take care of business and avoid a trap-game stumble on Wednesday.

For the Lakers' injury report, only Quentin Grimes (right finger sprain) is listed as questionable.

As for the Bucks, no injury report has been released since they'll be playing on the second night of a back-to-back. They're coming off a 32-point loss against the New York Knicks.

It's also worth noting that Tyler Herro (right knee contusion) didn't play on Tuesday.

#2726. Stephen A Smith says the Minnesota Vikings should be ‘ashamed’ of themselves

The Minnesota Vikings attempted to solve their issues at quarterback on Tuesday by trading for Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders.

It is a return to Minnesota for Cousins after the quarterback departed the organisation back in 2023 to join the Atlanta Falcons. It is a trade that Minnesota have made in an attempt to try and play complementary football, given that their defense has considerably outplayed their offense.

How big a difference Cousins will make remains to be seen, considering he failed to beat any of the five contenders this season with the Raiders. Although the Vikings are pushing to go all the way this season, Stephen A. Smith has heavily criticised the organisation for how they've handled the QB position over recent years.

The Vikings clearly have a defensive unit capable of making it to the Super Bowl, but there has been a lot left to desire on offense. It has been a merry-go-round in the quarterback department over recent months in Minnesota and Smith has been left far from impressed.

"I went on the air this morning [Tuesday] and said Justin Jefferson should demand to be traded, and I meant it. And I hope that had an impact, with the Minnesota Vikings going out and getting Kirk Cousins. They should be ashamed of themselves that they allowed it to get to this point," Smith said on his YouTube channel.

"I didn't even bring up Addison and Hockenson and how bad those brothers are when they've got a quarterback. You don't have cats like that on your squad and not have a quarterback to throw them the football. Shameful, shameful. So maybe they're making amends by getting Kirk Cousins. We shall see."

Ever since the Vikings allowed Sam Darnold to leave the building for the Seattle Seahawks, the organisation has struggled to nail down their next quarterback. J.J. McCarthy has since been moved on, Kyler Murray has failed to impress, and Carson Wentz is what he is.

For a team that has a blue-chip receiver on their roster like Justin Jefferson, it is clear that Smith feels the Vikings are fortunate the WR has provided the organisation with so much patience, given his own stats have taken a hit as a result of the quarterback situation.

Cousins is now 38 years of age, so he is unlikely to be the long-term solution in Minnesota. What lies ahead for the organisation over the long term at quarterback remains a complete mystery.

#2725. "Call it a day, Manu!" – Bayern legend urges Neuer to call time on his career

Germany goalkeeping icon Sepp Maier believes it's time for Manuel Neuer to hang up his gloves at the end of the season.

Asked by Sport1 what he would tell Neuer if the Bayern goalkeeper called him to ask whether he should continue playing beyond the summer of 2027, Maier responded:

“I would tell him, ‘Call it a day, Manu!’ You have given football an incredible amount, you have won everything and you no longer have anything to prove to anyone.

“Manuel has had an incredible career and revolutionised goalkeeping. But at some point, the body no longer holds up the way you would like it to. And even Manuel Neuer can't stop that moment from coming,” Maier also said in the interview, while stressing that the 40-year-old has to make the decision for himself.

Having already missed several games this season, Neuer suffered another setback in Saturday's 2-1 win over Mainz, with a tendon tear expected to keep him out for several weeks.

With Neuer having spent so much time on the sidelines, 23-year-old Jonas Urbig – widely regarded as his successor at Bayern – has already made eight appearances this season.

Following Neuer's latest injury setback, some have suggested that Bayern should make Urbig their first-choice goalkeeper already, and Maier also weighed in on the debate:

“At some point, you have to take that step. Manuel is 40 years old and Jonas Urbig is the future of Bayern Munich. But you cannot simply write Manuel off either. If he is fit and performing well, he should be allowed to play. However, Bayern need to make a clear decision sooner rather than later. This constant back-and-forth does neither goalkeeper any favours,” he said.

“When Manuel is fully fit, I still consider him one of the best goalkeepers. His experience, presence and understanding of the game are truly exceptional. But the crucial question is: how often is he still fully fit? Being world-class is no use if your body can no longer keep up. And Jonas Urbig is doing a good job. You shouldn't underestimate him either.”

#2724. Celtics rout 76ers in first matchup between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown

Celtics rout 76ers in first matchup between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area

Round 1 of the new-look Sixers vs. the new-look Celtics decisively went Boston's way on Tuesday night.

In the first meeting between the teams since the July trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia and Paul George to Boston, the Celtics earned a 123-101 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

The Sixers dropped to 9-3 and the Celtics improved to 9-2.

George was the game's brightest star, scoring 36 points on 14-for-22 shooting. Jayson Tatum added 21 points.

Tyrese Maxey's 24 points led the Sixers. Brown was hampered by foul trouble in his heavily anticipated first outing against Tatum. He posted 13 points, five rebounds and two assists in 26 minutes.

The Sixers will host the Raptors on Thursday night. Here are observations on their blowout loss to the Celtics:

To no one's surprise, Brown and Tatum guarded each other to open the night.

VJ Edgecombe defended a former teammate in George, who scored Boston's first four points with a pair of pure jumpers. On the other end, Maxey made the Sixers' first three field goals.

Judging by volume, the home fans cared most about the much-scrutinized Brown vs. Tatum matchup. The crowd was excited early when Brown snagged a steal and then dished to Maxey for a fast-break three-pointer. The fans also dialed up the noise when Brown sized up Tatum in isolation. He wound up dribbling the ball off his foot and out of bounds. Tatum pointed to signal it was Celtics ball.

Boston's star forward had a productive first quarter, posting 11 points. He scored an easy two when he used a back screen to break free from Brown and convert a layup that put the Celtics up 11-7. Boston began 9 for 12 from the floor as a team.

As for Brown, he sat shortly after being called for his second foul with 6:48 left in the first quarter.

Brown re-entered at the start of the second quarter. The Sixers still struggled to eat into Boston's lead.

A Sam Hauser triple extended the Celtics' advantage to 12 points. There was some audible frustration in the building after Brown missed two free throws on the next possesion.

The Sixers' deficit hit 16 points on a Hugo Gonzalez jumper. Meanwhile, the Sixers missed 12 of their first 14 three-point tries. While some of those shots were open looks that simply didn't go down, the Sixers also rushed up several contested jumpers before they made Boston's defense do serious work.

In the bigger picture, it wouldn't be remotely surprising if shooting stands out as a weak area for the Sixers come the trade deadline. They entered the game ranked 27th in the NBA in three-point frequency outside of garbage time and 22nd in three-point accuracy, according to Cleaning the Glass.

Joel Embiid (16 points, six rebounds) had an injury scare late in the second quarter when he fell hard after missing a layup in transition. He rose gingerly and limped through the final 30 seconds or so of the first half.

The Sixers' star big man was fine to start the third quarter and even drained a long-overdue three on the opening possession. He'd been in a terrible outside shooting slump (3 for 32 from deep on the season) before that shot.

Brown's foul trouble persisted. He picked up his fourth personal with 10:40 to go in the third quarter.

The Sixers stormed back without him and their defense played a large role. After LeBron James rumbled in for a layup, Dean Wade stonewalled Payton Pritchard on the perimeter to force a shot-clock violation. Wade later canned a three to even the contest at 76-all.

The Celtics responded and Tatum led the charge. His third-quarter exploits included a highlight slam on James and a top-of-the-key three to build Boston's lead back up to nine points.

Pritchard buried a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter and the Celtics' advantage kept growing. George celebrated a triple that stretched his team's lead to 100-82. The Sixers' spirits were considerably lower as they headed to their bench for a timeout. As a Sixer, George only had one higher-scoring game (39 points) than his performance Tuesday.

George and Tatum were each excellent in Philadelphia. Outside of Maxey, who finished 8 for 12 from the field, the Sixers didn't receive similar games from their stars.

Brown will be back in Boston on Jan. 21 when the Sixers visit the Celtics. He'll try to even the score.

#2723. Week 10 Fantasy Football Mailbag: Should Managers Add Fernando Mendoza?

The NFL trade deadline is in the rearview mirror, and a few moves altered the fantasy football landscape. Kirk Cousins reunited with the Minnesota Vikings, Keenan Allen was traded to the San Francisco 49ers, and Josh Downs was sent to the Kansas City Chiefs.

In this week's installment of our fantasy football mailbag, which questions are eating away at managers?

Note: Feel free to reach out to me on Twitter so I can answer your fantasy football questions in future articles.

All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) practices before the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

With Cousins traded to the Vikings, the Fernando Mendoza era is set to begin for the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10. Ahead of his first career start, should fantasy managers add Mendoza?

In superflex leagues, fantasy managers should scoop up Mendoza if he's available. While Mendoza is viable in deeper leagues for desperate managers, it may be worth waiting to start him.

Mendoza will be thrown into the fire to begin his career, facing the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos in his first two starts. The Seahawks and Broncos are both 10th or better in dropback EPA allowed.

Things get easier for Mendoza after the Raiders' bye in Week 13, as he'll face the Los Angeles Chargers, Tennessee Titans, and Arizona Cardinals in three of his final five games. The Titans and Cardinals are 27th or worse in dropback EPA allowed, while the Chargers are 17th.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson (18) warms up before the game against the Buffalo Bills at U.S. Bank Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Justin Jefferson, Josh Downs, and Keenan Allen were the WRs most affected during the NFL trade deadline. Where should each of them rank moving forward?

Entering Week 10, Jefferson is the WR31 in fantasy points per game (11.9). However, with Cousins throwing passes to Jefferson again, there's no reason to rank Jefferson outside the top 10 WRs anymore.

Jefferson was the WR2 in fantasy points per game (21.7) in 2022 with Cousins as his QB.

Downs is the WR61 in fantasy points per game (8.3) playing in a below-average Indianapolis Colts offense. But with Downs going from Daniel Jones to Patrick Mahomes, Downs could soon move into the WR3 or flex range.

While Downs' metrics are disappointing this year, there's a non-zero chance he becomes the No. 1 target for Mahomes over Rashee Rice before the season concludes.

The 49ers have been shorthanded at WR in recent weeks, so Allen is primed for a decent-sized role immediately. If Mike Evans and/or Deebo Samuel are inactive again in Week 10, Allen could be a WR3 or flex option as a slot target for Brock Purdy.

Once San Francisco's wideouts are healthy, Allen and Samuel will be ranked similarly, while Evans would still be the top option in the passing game.

Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride (85) spikes the ball after a touchdown catch against the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect

The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals are both dealing with a bevy of injuries on offense, limiting the viable pass-catchers available. With the Rams and Cardinals facing each other in Week 10, can managers trust any pass-catchers from either team?

On the Rams side of the equation, Tyler Higbee is in the best position to succeed with Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Terrance Ferguson sidelined. While I'd avoid starting any of the Rams WRs, rookie CJ Daniels is a name to watch if he gets more playing time.

As for the Cardinals, Trey McBride is still a must-start TE, though his ceiling could be lowered with rookie Carson Beck expected to start at QB. At the same time, Michael Wilson is out for the rest of the season, which could be viewed as a positive or negative for McBride managers.

Amid other injuries at WR, the Cardinals will trot out a wideout trio of Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, and Devin Duvernay. None of them should be trusted in any format right now.

Hopefully everyone's fantasy football squads enjoy plenty of success in Week 10!

#2721. Sixers Bell Ringer: Rough night for all as Sixers crushed by barrage of Celtics triples

Bell Ringer Standings:Tyrese Maxey – 3.5Jaylen Brown – 2.5VJ Edgecombe – 2Joel Embiid – 1LeBron James – 1Anfernee Simons – 1

Well, that could have gone better. The Philadelphia 76ers were absolutely buried by a barrage of three-pointers from the Boston Celtics and fell 123-101 on Tuesday night.

It was a highlight anticipated matchup of Eastern Conference teams, with Jaylen Brown facing his former squad for the first time as a member of the Sixers. This also meant the return of Paul George, who now sports Celtics green… and he made himself known in this one, to say the least.

It was a rough first half for the Sixers, who looked completely flat offensively and lacked any foundation on defense. They'd manage a bucket, then immediately allow the Celtics to knock down another three. Looking back, Philadelphia were fortunate to only be down 11 points going into halftime. A minor miracle.

The Sixers came out a much better team in the third, finally knocking down some shots and chipping away at the Celtics lead to bring things back even… for a moment.

Boston stayed red hot from beyond the arc, and rebuilt their lead to nine going into the final frame. And they just didn't stop. Three after three after three. They hit nine threes on a run spanning from late in the third into the fourth. It was relentless. Meanwhile, the Sixers didn't score for nearly five whole minutes to start the fourth. Hard to keep a game close with that kind of math going against you!

The Sixers are off Wednesday night and will return on Thursday evening hosting the Toronto Raptors.

Until then, let's get to the Bell Ringer, if we must.

Tyrese Maxey: 24 points, 1 rebound, 4 assists

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

Tyrese Maxey got his night going quickly with a 3-for-3 start from the floor for eight quick points in the first. He ended up leading the Sixers after their lackluster first half with 12 points on 4-for-6 field goal, 1-for-1 three-point shooting. It was a rough first half for really every Sixer, but his contributions were part of why they were only down a dozen at the break. And he wasn't done. In the third, things really started to heat up for Maxey, who put up another dozen points in the frame with some silky smooth 4-for-5 field goal shooting to help give the Sixers their only real taste of momentum all game, including knocking down two big threes.

It wasn't nearly enough to survive the Celtics absolutely onslaught from long range, but Maxey was the only Sixer to shoot well throughout the night and was critical to the brief, fleeting moment the Sixers looked like they might turn this one around.

Maxey finished leading the Sixers with 24 points on 8-for-12 field goal, 3-for-4 three-point shooting with a rebound and four assists.

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

Honestly, Dean Wade was one of the only players I thought put in good minutes throughout the entire first half, rather than just a moment here or there. Wade put up some incredible defense on Jayson Tatum at times in the first frame, was grabbing boards left and right and even knocked down a few buckets. At the half, he actually led the Sixers in +/- as a 0. Not bad for a game they trailed by 11 at the time. He got right back to work in the third, putting up more some extremely-respectable defense and adding a triple that briefly tied the game up.

Wade has done this a few games now where he really just does all the little fundamental things right. Even if it's just going up for every defensive board he can get his hands on, or just putting up solid defense that never really shows on basic stat sheet, to simply knocking in a few points when the opportunity presents itself. Wade has been an absolute asset for the Sixers off the bench and he deserves some recognition for it.

Wade finished with eight points and nine rebounds (two offensive). And that's part of what I mean, it hardly sounds like a crazy stat line, but he was truly one of the more consistently productive players for Philadelphia all night.

VJ Edgecombe: 8 points, 4 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal, 1 block

(Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images)

Of the rough first half performances from the Sixers, VJ Edgecombe put up one the of the least-rough. Thinking positive, people! The sophomore filled the stat sheet with six points, three rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block by the break. Edgecombe came out to start the second half and hit a truly insane finish through contact from Neemias Queta. It was part of the only little run the Sixers could really string together tonight in the third frame.

The bar was pretty low tonight, so I honestly was giving a nomination to VJ regardless just to show off this play. It was one of the very few exciting moments of the night for Philadelphia. Edgecombe finished with eight points, four rebounds, five assists, a steal and a block.

#2720. Cardinals post-NFL trade deadline moves & workouts

The Arizona Cardinals weren't buyers or sellers at the NFL trade deadline. They simply stood pat, and life – and the schedule – moved along.

It was assumed that at least two Cardinals players would be shipped off to new homes, but that never happened.

RELATED: CARDINALS TURN DOWN TRADE OFFER FOR BUDDA

So, after the trade deadline, there was plenty of activity with the franchise.

The big news is that the Cardinals announced they had placed QB Gardner Minshew on IR. There was some question as to whether Minshew would need to be placed on IR, or if his torn UCL in his throwing arm wasn't as serious as first thought. But it was. The word is that it could be season-ending, but that has not been confirmed.

Arizona also placed WR Michael Wilson officially on IR as expected. He injured his neck on the fourth offensive play during last week's game against the Seattle Seahawks. But get this: He played the entire game. One word: Ironman.

Obviously, both of these injuries are crippling events for the offense. This side of the ball is already without OT Paris Johnson, WRs Jalen Brooks and Kendrick Bourne, OG Chase Bisontis, RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner, and TE Tip Reiman.

The only other roster move is that WR Phillip Dorsett was signed to the practice squad.

Dorsett (5'-10", 185 pounds) was a beast in college at Miami, where he was clocked at 4.33 in the 40. As a senior, he led the conference in average yards per catch (24.2) and touchdowns (10). He was drafted 29th overall in the first round of the 2015 NFL Draft by the Indianapolis Colts, but after two seasons, he was traded to the New England Patriots for QB Jacoby Brissett.

Arizona is his 10th NFL club. Now age 33, Dorsett has been signed to six different practice squads. He did not appear in any regular-season NFL games in 2024, 2025, or this year. Obviously, the receiver position is a need for the Cardinals. Dorsett joins WR Shedrick Jackson and WR/KR James Proche on the practice squad.

Center Hjalte Froholdt is on concussion protocol from the Seahawks game. That usually takes 10 days to get clearance, which most likely means he won't be available for the home contest this weekend against the Los Angeles Rams. The depth chart lists Kingsley Eguakun as his backup. He has played in seven NFL games with two starts.

On Tuesday, while the league was swirling with trade news, the Cardinals worked out five players:

At one time, Rush (6'-3", 224 pounds) was considered the heir apparent to the starting quarterback position with the Dallas Cowboys. This is his ninth NFL season, and he has been a member of three NFL clubs. He has played in 44 games with 18 starts, thrown for 3,995 yards with a 60.8% completion ratio, and thrown 21 TDs to 18 picks. He appeared in two games for the Atlanta Falcons this year before being released on October 19.

Siemian (6'-3", 220 pounds) is a former seventh-round selection of the Denver Broncos who eventually became the starter in his second year after Peyton Manning retired. He ended up on IR after Week 15, and then was traded to the Minnesota Vikings for a fifth-round pick, but never played backing up Kirk Cousins. He ended up on three other NFL rosters. He was placed on two practice squads in 2023 and 2024, and hasn't played a single down since the 2023 season.

Meiga (6'-4", 201 pounds) played for Coastal Carolina with a 16.7 average yards per reception and went undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft. He signed with the Seahawks and then the Carolina Panthers. He is Canadian-born. Meiga has not appeared in any regular-season games.

Pancol (6'-3", 205 pounds) went undrafted in 2025 after a good career at Duke. He signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars and was waived in August with an injury designation as part of final roster cuts. He then signed with the Indianapolis Colts, who placed him on their practice squad but he was not re-signed for 2026. He was placed on the practice squad of the Denver Broncos on October 27, then waived on November 3. He has not appeared in any regular-season games.

Out of the five, Dorsett was the only player signed to a deal. Often, teams bring in guys to update their free agent database in the event a player (or two) becomes injured, but in this case, both the quarterback and receiver positions were recently hit with the injury bug, so talent was brought in for a closer look.

At the movies, sometimes there is a short little blurb right after the credits have ended. Every CG cartoon has one, as do the horror and superhero flicks. So, this is our blurb for those who are still reading.

RB Dameon Pierce was a fourth-round draft pick of the Houston Texans back in 2022 and became a Pro Bowl alternate that same year. His highlight was a 98-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in 2023. After his four-year rookie contract expired in 2025, the Texans decided to keep Nick Chubb instead. Pierce was signed by the Kansas City Chiefs to their practice squad and then was elevated to the main roster in late December.

In free agency this year, he signed a one-year $1.29 million deal with the Philadelphia Eagles, but was a last-day cut and then signed to their practice squad. Before Week 6, Pierce was elevated to the main roster. He suffered a hamstring injury, and Philly released him with an injury settlement.

He is now a free agent. Seven teams have reached out to his agent: San Francisco, Miami, Tennessee, Baltimore, Jacksonville, Carolina, and the Cardinals.

Arizona has three running backs on its active roster: Tyler Allgeier, Bam Knight, and Evan Hull, plus veteran Jerome Ford on the practice squad. They are expecting James Conner to return at some point.

What does this mean for the team to go fishing on Pierce? Knight has had some injury issues, but with the availability of Ford, why the looksy? Does this indicate that the team doesn't have any confidence in Conner's return this season? Hmmm……

#2719. Ben Johnson says Bears' red-zone defense won game vs. Bucs

As much as the Chicago Bears identity under Ben Johnson has become their high-powered offense led by quarterback Caleb Williams, but now their defense is tarting to come around following the acquisition of All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

In their Week 9 victory over the Buccaneers, it was the Bears offense that held the team back, with Williams throwing four interceptions but ultimately, the defense won the game with Jaylon Johnson's pick-six of Baker Mayfield.

The Bears defense as a whole only allowed two touchdown, holding Tampa Bay's offense to just 2-5 in the red zone, in a game where they had to come up big with their backs against the wall. Bucky Irving and the Buccaneers ground game has been on fire over the last few weeks, and their 126 rushing yards helped carry their offense for most of the night, but Chicago's head coach was very proud of his defense.

After the win, Johnson said he believes the team's defensive performance in the red zone was the reason they came out victorious.

"I think that was really the story of the game was those guys stepping up and it was all the way up until that last one that they finally broke through and scored the touchdown," Johnson said. "But for the four previous ones, I thought our defense did an outstanding job rising the occasion. They don't bat an eye, they don't blink. That's certainly what (Defensive Coordinator Dennis Allen) DA preaches on that side of the ball, but I think those guys take a lot of pride in that as well. And we needed that tonight."

Dennis Allen has definitely shined over the last few games in Chicago's victories, especially the last two weeks since the arrival of Jeffery Simmons. If the Bears showed anything in their Week 9 victory, it's that they're now finding balance that if their offense can't carry the successful workload on their own, the defense will certainly be ready to step up and earn the win.

#2717. NFL Secret Superstars: 3 under-the-radar AFC standouts from Week 9

Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it's the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they're needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they're playing in a smaller market, and the media isn't appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they're hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it's always possible that a wayward coach hasn't quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team.

Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here.

Here are our AFC Secret Superstars for Week 9 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven't yet, download the new SB Nation app, so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are!

(All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Focus, Sports Info Solutions, and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated).

Is your offense better and more dangerous with a truly explosive running back? Obviously, yes. If you have a Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs, or James Cook, your offense is going to cook in ways others can't if they don't have one of those rare backs who's always a threat to take one to the house.

But if you don't have such a back — and there are only a handful in the NFL at any given time — what do you do then? The second-best option is to have at least one back who can sustain drives with consistent power, and whatever agility and straight-line speed is in the skill set.

This is why Sean Payton's Denver Broncos selected Washington back Jonah Coleman with the 108th overall pick in the fourth round of the 2026 draft. In his final college season, the 5'9", 228-pound Coleman ran the ball 157 times for 758 yards (4.8 yards per carry), 15 touchdowns, 37 forced missed tackles, 20 runs of 10 or more yards, and 11 runs of 15 or more yards. But all anybody wanted to talk about with Coleman was his alleged lack of explosiveness and burst, which I found interesting based on my own tape study. The guy wasn't running 4.2 40-yard dashes on the field, but big plays happened pretty frequently.

Coleman also caught 31 passes on 34 targets for 346 yards and two touchdowns in 2025, which set him up well for Payton's offense, where the backs need to be receivers.

Coleman's NFL transition was slowed by an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September, but he's developed into a force multiplier over the last two weeks. He had 104 total yards on 15 touches against the Kansas City Chiefs in a 28-24 Week 8 win, and last Sunday against the Carolina Panthers in a 26-21 win, Coleman ran 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown, with three forced missed tackles. He also caught four passes for 31 yards. Did he have a single play over 10 yards? No he didn't, but over and over when he was handed the rock, Coleman was able to make Denver's drives easier by creating first downs, and making first downs easier for others by getting the Broncos in favorable down-and-distance situations.

"We had those glimpses in the spring and in training camp and in the preseason," Payton said of Coleman on Nov. 4. "The one thing that was unique about him is oftentimes, you don't get to see [young running backs] in third-down protection plans, but he was someone that we had quite a bit of tape on. Advanced protection plans, and he's built to handle the blitz. It's one thing to know who I have, but then also to be strong enough to do it. I would say that there were three backs [in the draft] — we just saw one of them [Coleman] that we really had visions for. Each one may be a little different, but his versatility, you don't get to stamp that with a lot of rookie backs that you feel like they're going to develop into. We saw enough that we felt like he was going to be a good third-down protecting back as well with the way he was built."

"I think he's playing really well with confidence. He's a very intelligent young running back. What sticks out the most is he can handle a lot. You can put a lot on his plate. After we learned that R.J. Harvey wasn't going to play last week, he got a little bit more of the bulk of R.J.'s stuff. It's impressive to see him be able to be used in a lot of different ways. When he gets in there, he's a natural runner. That's what he's drafted for. That's the position he plays. It's the out of the backfield stuff that I think is making a good impression on us right now."

Smart coaches and personnel people will tell you to avoid focusing on what a player can't do — instead, focus on the potential. Jonah Coleman won't blow you away with RedZone highlights, but when it comes to value for his offense, that's relatively irrelevant — and it's great that he's landed with a team that understands.

After the Texans blew the Los Angeles Chargers out of SoFi Stadium in their 44-22 shellacking of the NFL's only winless team, the conversation turned to quarterback C.J. Stroud's amazing day (21 of 35 for 385 yards, five touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 125.5), Tank Dell's first touchdown catch since Week 16 of the 2024 season, and Nico Collins' insane touchdown catch over cornerback Tarheeb Still.

But the Texan who caught two touchdown passes in that game was Kayshon Boutte, the former New England Patriot who was traded to Houston on Aug. 24 for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick. Boutte hadn't been one of the Texans' primary targets this season — he had 15 catches on 25 targets for 194 yards and no touchdowns on the season before Sunday — and head coach DeMeco Ryans was quite happy about Boutte breaking out with four catches on five targets for 125 yards and those two scores.

"I've really been working with the offense trying to get them to get Boutte a pass where he can stay up and run it in for a touchdown—he did that today," Ryans said postgame. "A lot of his catches he's made in the previous weeks were tough catches on the sideline, but this time he was actually able to run one for a touchdown. On that particular play to see [WR] Nico [Collins] down the field blocking and see [TE] Dalton [Schultz] down the field blocking, that's probably what I'm most proud of on that play. Guys really selling out for each other."

Well, now the 3-5 Texans have that to add to the overall arsenal as they try to overcome their unexpectedly rough (0-4) start to the season.

The Jaguars are the best team people aren't talking about enough (they currently rank first in overall DVOA for the first time in franchise history), and a primary reason for that is a defense that is the NFL's most underrated. Anthony Campanile's defense (remember that name; Campanile is on a head coach track) ranked third in Defensive DVOA before they traded for Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, New Orleans Saints IDL Davon Godchaux, and Philadelphia Eagles IDL Jordan Davis.

Jags general manager James Gladstone learned all about "F Them Picks" during his time in the Los Angeles Rams' front office from 2016 through 2024, and he has good reason to go all out now. This is a legitimate Super Bowl contender, and the guys that Campanile already had on his roster have played above their name recognition.

Perhaps the man whose national awareness lags farthest behind his actual achievements is linebacker Ventrell Miller. The 2023 fourth-round pick out of Florida lost his entire rookie season to a torn Achilles tendon in the preseason, and had to overcome other ailments in 2024 and 2025, but the fully healthy version of Mr. Miller has been quite the revelation. On the season, Miller has a sack, eight pressures, 35 solo tackles, 23 stops, three tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. In coverage, he's allowed 17 catches on 24 targets for 128 yards, no touchdowns, no interceptions, four pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 83.3.

Miller was at his best in last Thursday's 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens, showing his skills at the line of scrimmage, and at the second level.

"He's done a really good job overall," Campanile said of Miller back on Sept. 24. "He's a guy you can rely on to set the tone physically for the defense. And that's one thing that I feel like he's done over the first two games. He's looking to improve, he's trying to do extra. And I think all of his teammates see that, and that's been a good thing for our defense."

An extremely good thing for a Jaguars defense that is on the way up. Ventrell Miller has become a top-tier NFL linebacker at the perfect time for his team.

#2714. Andy Reid’s Tenured Professor Era Sparks Chiefs Fans Debate

Andy Reid has entered a phase where he acts like a tenured professor who is tired of student questions. The Kansas City Chiefs head coach has made it clear that he does not enjoy answering the same inquiries from the media week after week. This attitude was on full display after the team defeated the New York Jets 35-12 on Sunday. While the win ended a two-game losing streak, the postgame interaction highlighted a growing divide between the coach and the people asking about his decisions.

The coach has plenty of passion for his players and still shows creativity on the field, but his public demeanor has changed. He now tells reporters exactly what he will and will not discuss. This shift has led to frustration among fans who feel he is avoiding accountability for recent struggles. The situation has become a weekly occurrence where Reid cuts off questions before they are fully formed, creating an air of dismissal toward the press corps.

One of the main topics Reid refuses to discuss is the job security of kicker Harrison Butker. The veteran kicker has struggled with long-distance field goals this season. Since 2024, Butker has made only 45 percent of his field goals from 50 yards or more. At a 69.5 percent rate, every other NFL kicker is converting these attempts. Despite these poor numbers, Reid told reporters he would not make any decisions on the spot during the press conference.

Reid opened his remarks by stating that he knew he would be asked about Butker. He said he would address the situation as the week goes on and that there is no need for reporters to ask the question again. He made it clear that he would look at everything before making a move. This response was accepted by the media, as not a single reporter pushed him on the issue during the session.

Following Butker's failure to convert two additional field goals before halftime in the matchup versus the Jets, reluctance to tackle the kicker's performance has emerged. One of those misses was rendered moot because an offside penalty was called on the defense. Reid knew the questions would be coming, yet he chose to shut down the conversation early. This approach suggests he is protecting the player or perhaps avoiding the scrutiny that comes with making a high-profile change.

Another source of irritation for Reid is the constant questioning about left tackle Josh Simmons. A back injury sustained in mid-August caused the Chiefs player to miss the final two preseason games. Reid initially insisted the injury was minor, which became a point of discussion when Simmons missed the first regular-season game. By the time the team entered their bye week in Week 5, Simmons had not played a single snap despite being on the active roster.

Progress stalled further when a bulging disc in his back worsened the situation. He was eventually placed on injury reserve, ensuring he remains sidelined through Week 11 at the minimum. The will-he-or-won't-he nature of the update kept reporters confused and fans frustrated. Reid played coy most of the time, giving indirect and vague answers that only brought about more scrutiny.

Reid clarified his stance on confronting the reality of the injury during one update. He told reporters, according to Arrowhead Addict, "I hope this isn't asked to me every week. I mean, let's just put this to rest. He'll take care of that. This isn't that big of a story." His desire to end the line of questioning shows how much he dislikes the repetitive nature of injury updates. The communication from the team always felt indirect, which only fueled more speculation about the true state of the player's health.

Reid also made a controversial decision to bench Kingsley Suamataia at left guard in Week 8 against the Denver Broncos. He decided to play Mike Caliendo instead of the rookie lineman. Suamataia was benched for the second time, after being substituted in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders. The move signaled a lack of confidence in the young player's ability to protect the quarterback in key situations.

Fans and analysts have pointed to these benching decisions as evidence that the offensive line is not gelling. The inconsistency at the guard position has led to more pressure on the quarterback and fewer running lanes for the ball carriers. Reid's choice to go with Caliendo suggests he believes the veteran can handle the job better than the rookie. However, the move has not stopped the criticism regarding the team's offensive execution.

The benching of Suamataia adds to the list of personnel decisions that have drawn scrutiny. It is part of a pattern where Reid makes changes that confuse the fanbase. The lack of a clear explanation for why the rookie was benched has left many wondering about the criteria for playing time. This uncertainty contributes to the feeling that the team is not operating with a clear plan.

The most notable moment of the press conference came after a failed quarterback sneak during the game. On a third-and-1 in the first quarter, Reid inserted backup quarterback Justin Fields to execute a sneak. The play failed to convert, and Fields fumbled the ball. The Jets recovered the fumble and capitalized with a field goal to take an early lead. This play marked the first quarterback sneak with an actual quarterback for Kansas City since 2019.

Reid blamed the media for the failure of the play. He joked that he felt pressured by reporters to call the sneak after they criticized him for not calling one in the previous game against Denver. This remark was made in a joking tone, but it highlighted his annoyance with the constant media scrutiny.

Reid explained that the play is difficult to perfect because it is hard to practice live. He stated, "Yeah, so listen, we've got to make sure—those are hard to practice live." He added that the quarterback sneak is hard to practice unless you do it in a game. He emphasized the need to get the two players on the same page and ensure the ball gets up first in the quarterback's hands. Despite the explanation, the failed play remains a coaching error in the eyes of many.

Fans have expressed strong frustration with Reid's handling of the situation. A fan commented that a scapegoat always exists to sidestep the actual issue, which they identify as Andy Reid. The fan noted that last year it was Matt Nagy, last week it was Mike Caliendo, and this week it will be Harrison Butker. This pattern of shifting blame has angered supporters who feel the coach is not taking responsibility for the team's struggles.

Reid's reaction to the botched play drew criticism from another fan who labeled it entirely unserious behavior. They wrote that Reid gave the team the most ill-prepared quarterback sneak ever and then told them to shut up about it. The fan argued that a head coach needs to take short-yardage futility much more seriously. This sentiment reflects a growing belief that the coach is not engaged in the details of the game.

One commenter stated bluntly that the average fan fails to grasp just how terrible Andy Reid is at his job. They called the situation pathetic. A different user contended that the failed sneak indicated a coaching issue rather than a reason to abandon the play entirely. They believe the team managed to turn a simple quarterback sneak into a turnover, which is a coaching failure. These comments show a deep divide between the coach and the fanbase.

Observers have likened Reid's present condition to Bill Belichick's concluding season in New England. OutKick's Bobby Burack wrote that Reid looks more confused than ever. He characterized Reid as an all-time great coach appearing utterly baffled by the current iteration of the NFL. This comparison draws parallels to Belichick's difficult 2023 season, where the Patriots finished 4-13.

Belichick's final season was a disaster, with the team ranking bottom of the NFL offensively and averaging just 13.9 points per game. Elimination from playoff contention happened with four weeks left. signifying their earliest removal since Belichick's first season. A 24-year streak featuring six Super Bowl titles concluded due to these struggles. Critics worry that Reid is heading down a similar path of decline.

The comparison is not just about wins and losses but about the decision-making process. Reid's reluctance to call quarterback sneaks and his vague injury updates mirror the confusion seen in Belichick's final year. The team has shown flashes of dominance, but the overall execution has been inconsistent. This uncertainty has led to questions about whether Reid can adapt to the modern game.

The team also left Sunday's win with significant injury concerns. A hamstring injury struck wide receiver Xavier Worthy during the game. Patrick Mahomes absorbed a hit to his right throwing elbow during a second-quarter strip-sack. Mahomes returned before halftime and finished the game, but he admitted he wasn't throwing the ball the way he wanted to early in the second half.

Worthy has struggled to become the reliable explosive option the team envisioned. Rashee Rice lost time to a hamstring injury, while Tyquan Thornton endured a significant ankle injury. Reid and Mahomes find it harder to maintain offensive momentum without a consistent downfield threat. When the running game fails to generate ground production, the receiving corps' lack of dependable output becomes a critical problem.

General manager Brett Veach admitted prior to the trade deadline that the Chiefs were investigating the receiver market.

#2713. Paul George flips off fan for ‘being an a–hole’ in Philadelphia return after Jaylen Brown blockbuster

George put up 36 points in the Celtics' 123-101 win over the Sixers on Tuesday night in Philadelphia in a highly anticipated matchup that pitted star players against their former teams.

The ex-Sixer and current Celtics star crouched down and then lifted his middle finger in the direction of a fan after he hit a 3-pointer.

The decision to allegedly antagonize George seemed like a questionable decision by the fan, considering the dominant game he had against his former team.

#2712. Bengals Film Room: Joe Burrow now a frontrunner for MVP?

The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show in Madrid, Spain, defeating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17. Quarterback Joe Burrow was 24 for 29 for 271 yards. He threw 3 touchdown passes and, most importantly, did not throw an interception this week.

Jordan Love currently leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 yards on the season. Burrow is currently second with 2,386 passing yards. It is important to note that Burrow has also played one less game than Jordan Love this year. Burrow has a better completion rate, completing an elite 74% of his passes this season. Burrow is also leading the league in touchdown passes, having thrown 23 of them already this season.

It isn't just the stats that are jumping out for Burrow; he is in full control of an explosive Cincinnati offense that is firing on all cylinders. Let's take a look at some of his biggest plays from the win against Atlanta.

After the Falcons drove down the field and scored a touchdown to start the game, Joe Burrow and the offense were able to answer right back. The biggest play of the drive came on a 47-yard touchdown strike to Ja'Marr Chase. The Bengals tried to hit that play last week, with Burrow not getting enough on the ball and ultimately throwing an interception. That wasn't the case this week, as he hit Chase in stride to help tie the game up 7-7.

After an Atlanta Falcons field goal, the Bengals offense was able to drive right down the field again. Burrow got some incredible catches from his wide receivers on this drive. The first one was a 7-yard completion to Tee Higgins on a third down that allowed the Bengals to keep the drive alive. Higgins caught the ball with strong hands in traffic. He was also being held on the ball, though no flag was thrown.

Not long after that completion, it was Ja'Marr Chase making a spectacular play for his quarterback. Burrow threw a pass a bit too far out in front of Ja'Marr. The defender thought he had an interception, until Ja'Marr decided to snag the ball out of the air with one hand. He immediately turned upfield for yards after the catch.

Burrow and the offense were able to get up to the line quickly after getting down to the 1-yard line on this drive. Burrow caught the Falcons off guard and called his own number for the quarterback sneak. He recorded his second rushing touchdown in as many weeks as a result. This score put the Bengals up 14-10.

After the defense forced a Falcons punt, Joe Burrow and the offense were back on the field for their third series of the game. They started the drive with Burrow going to Ja'Marr Chase once again. This time for a 31-yard catch-and-run.

Burrow displayed his toughness on a crucial third down during the drive. He had to scramble out to his right and was able to extend the play just long enough to get a patented Ja'Marr is down there somewhere pass off. Burrow got leveled on the play, but the result was a big completion to a diving Chase down the field for another first down.

With pressure coming off the left side of the line, Burrow was able to convert another crucial third down on this drive. He had to double clutch, but stood tall in the pocket and delivered a pass that only his receiver could catch. That receiver just so happened to be Ja'Marr Chase again, who made a spectacular extension for the ball while getting his feet down just in bounds in the process. The Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase connection was strong in the first half, with Chase going for over 140 receiving yards and a touchdown.

Speaking of quarterback-to-receiver connections that have been on fire all season, Joe Burrow found Tee Higgins for the touchdown to cap off this drive. Burrow threw a perfect strike to Higgins just inside the end zone. Tee once again displayed strong hands to extend the Bengals' lead to 21-10.

It isn't just the top two receivers that Burrow has been finding for big plays this season either. Dohnte Meyers had a big play last week to help the Bengals ultimately force overtime and get the victory against Tennessee. This week it wasn't as dramatic of a moment, but Burrow once again scrambled out and was able to hit Meyers for a big play before halftime. The Bengals would ultimately kick a field goal on this drive, making their lead 24-10 at halftime.

Burrow and the rest of the offense didn't have to do a whole lot the rest of the way, but after Atlanta cut the lead to 24-17 in the third quarter, they did need to put together another scoring drive. That is exactly what they were able to do. Maybe one of the most impressive plays of the game for Joe Burrow was the touchdown at the end of this one. He went through his progression, stood tough in the pocket, and delivered an absolute strike to Tee Higgins in the middle of the end zone. That touchdown put the Bengals back up by two scores, a lead that was too much to overcome for the Atlanta Falcons.

It is only halfway through the season, so there is a ton of football to be played. With that said, Joe Burrow is firmly in everyone's midseason conversations for MVP. It won't just be up to him to keep playing at the level he is; the defense will also have to find ways to continue helping to win games. The MVP award is typically going to be given to a player who is part of a team with a lot of regular-season wins. A win against Pittsburgh in primetime Sunday Night Football would ramp up the MVP talk even more.

#2710. NFL Secret Superstars, Week 9: 3 under-the-radar NFC standouts

Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it's the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they're needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they're playing in a smaller market, and the media isn't appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they're hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it's always possible that a wayward coach hasn't quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team.

Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here.

Here are our NFC Secret Superstars for Week 9 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven't yet, download the new SB Nation app, so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are!

(All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Focus, Sports Info Solutions, and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated).

I've always had a thing for undersized defensive tackles. From John Randle to Geno Atkins to Grady Jarrett to Aaron Donald and on and on, the whole "low man wins" thing has always made sense to me. Because if you have the chops to succeed in the NFL when you're not meeting any of the established size parameters, there must be something pretty special about you.

The Detroit Lions are well aware of this, and they've been well aware of this since they selected North Carolina State's Alim McNeill with the 72nd overall pick in the third round of the 2021 draft. It's why the Lions gave McNeill a four-year, $97 million contract extension with $55 million guaranteed in 2024, and 2026 may be the 6'2", 310-pound McNeill's best season yet. Overall, he has 5.5 sacks, 34 pressures, 14 stops, and a whole lot of chaos for opposing offensive guards when he's lined up at three-technique.

Against the Miami Dolphins and guards Kadyn Proctor and Jonah Savaiinaea in Sunday's 19-9 Lions win, McNeill was an absolute force, with a sack and four total pressures. Now, he's in exalted company among interior disruptors around the NFL — right up there with Jeffery Simmons of the Chicago Bears (more on him in a minute) and Zach Allen of the Denver Broncos.

As Dan Campbell has said, McNeill ties the whole thing together when it comes to Detroit's defensive line.

"Well, we talked about this a while back," Campbell said of McNeill on Nov. 6. "I mean, it's one of the reasons Mac is an impact player. If you can get push up the middle, first of all, he shuts down the run between he and [DL] Tyleik [Williams]. He's excellent against the run game. But then to be able to get an edge and create pressure, and push and make the quarterback move, that helps [EDGE Aidan Hutchinson] Hutch, and that helps [EDGE DJ] Wonnum, and our other guys, [DL Skyler Gill-Howard] Sky.

"So man, it's big. You get an edge guy and you get somebody in the middle, then man, it really opens up your pressure package. So that alone in itself, four-man rush, you can create some havoc. But now, when you do decide to bring some of these pressure packages, it helps significantly.

"So, Mac's doing a hell of a job. He's playing at a high level right now."

The Lions stand at 6-2 in an NFC North that has become one of the most competitive divisions in NFL history, and as they look to make sense of a defense that has been up and down (to say the least), Alim McNeill will continue to do his level best to keep the math solid.

Football is the most interdependent sport. Nobody can succeed without the efforts of others. And there are those few special players in the NFL who, at any given time, can not only blow you away with their own abilities, but who can also make those around them better.

The Bears' trade for Jeffery Simmons has done just that for a whole lot of Chicago defenders. Since Chicago sent 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, as well as a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Tennessee Titans for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick on October 28, a middling defense has morphed into the new Monsters of the Midway.

But it's tough to mention anybody who has benefited more from Simmons' arrival than linebacker Devin Bush. In wins over the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8, and in Chicago's 27-24 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night, Bush has used Simmons' status as the guy every opposing offense needs to worry about into his own status as someone who is closer in the rear view than he may appear. Bush was especially outstanding against the Bucs, with eight solo tackles, four stops, a tackle for loss, a quarterback hurry, and two pass breakups in coverage.

Basically, everywhere the Bucs wanted to be, Bush was there first. And he helped the Bears win a game in which their own offense had five or more turnovers — the first time they've done that since 2006, when they did it twice — once in a 23-13 Week 13 win over the Minnesota Vikings, and more famously in a 24-23 Week 6 win over the Arizona Cardinals that had Arizona coach Dennis Green getting all legendary at the podium after the fact.

As for Bush, the 2019 10th overall pick of the Pittsburgh Steelers who also had stints with the Seattle Seahawks and the Cleveland Browns before the Bears signed him to a three-year, $30 million contract with $21 million guaranteed. For the first time in his career (though he was very good with the Browns last season), Bush is looking like the guy the NFL always wanted him to be.

"I think he keeps getting better every week," Bears head coach Ben Johnson said of Bush after the Bucs win. "And off the cuff, we've got to look at this tape here, but this might have been his best game yet as a Bear. And we'll see if that stays true or not. But he's all over the place, playing physical when he's hitting guys. He's fast. He's a great coverage player. We already knew that. But I think his understanding of the defense is really what's allowing him to play instinctive, fast football right now."

That, and Jeffery Simmons, will get you there every time.

The Rams welcomed Myles Garrett back to the field on Sunday for the first time since Week 1 — and Garrett went off against the Washington Commanders for three sacks and eight total pressures — but the team's injury issues continue unabated in other areas. The two cornerbacks the team got in offseason acquisitions — Trent McDuffie (back) and Jaylen Watson (shoulder; season-ending) were unavailable for this game, which meant that Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes were the next men up. In Forbes' case, that made him a starter against the franchise that selected him with the 16th overall pick in the 2023 draft, and released him on Nov. 30, 2024.

It's obviously unusual for a team to jettison a first-round pick less than two years into the experiment, but Forbes' Washington tenure was a disappointment for all involved. The Rams signed him on Dec. 2, 2024, and started to help Forbes turn his career around. Not that it was a total reclamation story — the Rams still went after McDuffie and Watson to solidify a cornerback group that needed help — but Forbes proved to be willing and able when it was time to enter the octagon. In the 20-13 win that put the Rams at 5-4 on the season, Forbes allowed six catches on 10 targets for 19 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions, three pass breakups, a coverage tackle for loss, and an opponent passer rating of 97.9.

"Yeah I had this one circled," Forbes said postgame. "I was motivated to play them guys. They let me go two years ago, and I was just ready to go out there and show myself what I got."

"That I'm a ballplayer, and when I'm playing my best, I think I'm the best in the world."

McVay wasn't quite ready to go there, but he was impressed.

"I thought he was great. I thought he played tough. I thought he came up in run support. I thought he was sticky in coverage. [Pass Game Coordinator/Defensive Backs Coach] Jimmy Lake does such a great job with that back end as a whole. I thought he and [CB] Josh Wallace were really… they were great for us today. Obviously, [Commanders QB] Jayden [Daniels] does such a great job of being able to extend plays. They got a lot of different guys that can make some plays, and I was really proud of Emmanuel Forbes. He did a good job today."

With the Dream Team stuff out the window, the Rams are just trying to maintain hope for the postseason. It obviously helps when their backups need to play like more than backups, and they do just that. And it was nice for Forbes to let his old team see what he's learned.
