#2706. Jaylen Brown snubbed Jayson Tatum before tipoff. His night against the Celtics only got worse

PHILADELPHIA — The final blow to the 76ers' chest — and their ego — came with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, as Paul George held his follow-through in front of his former bench and Jayson Tatum stretched his wings toward his teammate in celebration.

In stark contrast, Jaylen Brown's confusion over a busted coverage was plastered all over his face as he and the veteran, star-studded bunch shuffled back to their seats before the white flag was raised. What should have been a hotly contested duel had flamed out rather quickly, with hundreds of fans heading for the exits and a blowout in full effect.

"I'm a bit frustrated, honestly," Brown said following the 123-101 defeat. "I wanted to perform better for my team. Foul trouble kind of derailed me a little bit, but it happens. It's unfortunate but you gotta just move on to the next."

For weeks, the sheer build-up to Tuesday night essentially guaranteed an emotional apex. Cryptic messages, subtle shots and narratives built on both sides of the Tatum-Brown divide dominated headlines, airwaves and basketball discourse. Something was bound to give.

But even in that, Brown's emotions quite possibly got the best of him. Seconds before tipoff, after the tidal wave of boos, tension and apprehension had consumed the building, Brown had a golden opportunity to bury the hatchet as Tatum approached him near midcourt. An embrace, nod or handshake — something to acknowledge the near-decade relationship between the two — was set up perfectly. Instead, Brown chose in that moment to ignore Tatum as he tapped his former teammate's arm and chest twice.

It didn't end there. Brown used every opportunity he had to latch onto Tatum like an All-Pro cornerback, at times not even recognizing the ongoing action around him. When he received the ball, he put his head down and charged at opposing defenders recklessly, unable to generate rhythm — and the rampant roars from the Philly faithful only compounded Brown's downhill desperation and aggression. (Brown recorded his second-highest first-quarter usage rate this season, paired poorly with a 28.6 turnover rate.) A failure to find an offensive groove carried over to the other side of the ball, with Brown giving away cheap fouls, forcing him to sit and ultimately limiting him to just 25 minutes. His final tally told the story better than anything else could: 13 points, four turnovers and a game-worst minus-27.

"I'm just focused on coming out and doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else was, to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson, he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics, they executed and shot the hell out of the ball. They were the better team tonight."

The frustration was evident for Jaylen Brown, who struggled with foul trouble and turnovers in Philadelphia's blowout loss to the Celtics on Tuesday night.

To add insult to injury, it was Tatum and George who looked like they had played for nine years together instead of the three weeks. Boston has found a way to harmonize the pair's similar skill sets, as both combine usage (100th and 91st percentiles, respectively) with creation chops (98th and 87th percentiles). One of George's underrepresented qualities is his ability to assimilate within different ecosystems while not detracting from the order of operations. The Celtics have outscored opponents by 33 points in the 162 minutes both have shared the floor, a promising early sign for the league's No. 2 team in net rating. Both George and Tatum can play off the other, whether it's darting around screens and relocating, spacing the floor or drawing defenses to one side of the floor. The pair accounted for 18 of Boston's 49 attempted 3s, a hand-in-glove fit for Mazzulla ball — in addition to 56 points, 9 treys, 11 rebounds and 5 assists, feasting upon their prey. Beef. Lamb chops. Gravy.

For Brown, the conversation will continue surrounding how the former Finals MVP truly fits within the 76ers' structure. And it's not just that he's converting shots and handling the ball at rates not seen in over seven years, it's that his entire offensive makeup has changed drastically. Last season — the campaign Brown notoriously proclaimed as his favorite of his career — he operated as a lead ball-handler nearly 25 percent of the time on the floor, per Synergy tracking data. That volume has plummeted to just seven percent, with the bulk of his opportunities coming via spot-ups or in transition. Brown is certainly not as fluid or creative a playmaker as his former teammate Tatum or even George, but the sudden removal of opportunities certainly comes with its own trickle-down effects.

"He had a tough night," 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said. "They did a pretty good job of swarming him and sending multiple defenders."

The larger theme, one that will permeate this game, a rematch in Boston (which will be even more emotional for Brown) and beyond, is the fact that the 76ers' presumed path to playing in May and June also includes the Celtics. Both sit atop the Eastern Conference, having won nine games apiece, with some underlying separation already building on the coast. (Detroit and New York will certainly have something to say about how the final standings shake out; early November is a far cry from finality, but I'm more confident in seeing the demarcation between them and the likes of Toronto, Miami and Atlanta.)

It's why nights like these are important. They offer a window into the psyche of the world's most talented athletes, invoke emotional and mental challenges and push conversations forward. Brown will have more opportunities to even the score against his old coworker, but until he fully settles into his new surroundings, frustrating outings like this won't be outliers.

#2704. Klopp set to hold talks with Nmecha over controversial religious celebration

Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is expected to hold talks with Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha after the midfielder's controversial crown celebration sparked debate over the weekend, according to Bild.

When Nmecha bagged a brace in Borussia Dortmund's 2-1 win over SV Elversberg on Saturday, he celebrated by kneeling down, removing an imaginary crown and placing it on the ground.

The celebration is associated with the evangelical network “Ballers in God”, which LGBTQ+ organisations have classified as “Christian fundamentalist”, and its campaign “The King's Return”.

According to research by, among others, ARD's Monitor programme, parts of the religious group hold homophobic and anti-LGBTQ+ views and describe abortion as “Satan's plan”.

The celebration prompted Borussia Dortmund's Supporters Council to criticise the midfielder over the weekend and call on the club to clearly distance itself from evangelical networks.

Now, with Nmecha joining the German national team for the upcoming international fixtures as part of Jürgen Klopp's 24-man squad, a conversation with the coach about the celebration is reportedly on the cards.

German Football Association sporting director Rudi Völler addressed the issue on the podcast Kerners 11.

“Of course, there is freedom of religion and freedom of belief. Everyone is free to express their faith in their own way. Some people like it, others don't. Naturally, we will speak to him about it again, because it has now become a public issue. The most important thing with an issue like this is that you first have to understand it properly. We have to ensure that the processes surrounding these matters are handled correctly," Völler said, via Bild.

“So far, I can only say positive things about Felix. He did an outstanding job at the World Cup – not just as a footballer, but also in the way he behaved between matches. He is extremely popular with his teammates and is a thoroughly decent person.

“But I can understand the debate and that not everyone likes it. As I said, we will handle it in a similar way to Dortmund – we are in contact with them. But we shouldn't blow it out of proportion either. We will certainly speak to him about it.”

Nmecha also performed the celebration after scoring in Germany's 7-1 win over Curaçao at last summer's World Cup.

#2702. John Spytek: Fernando Mendoza passed every test, allowed us to make a hard decision

It took longer than it has for most quarterbacks drafted first overall, but Fernando Mendoza's time has come in Las Vegas.

Tuesday's trade of Kirk Cousins means that Mendoza is now the No. 1 quarterback for the Raiders and he'll make his first NFL start in Sunday's game against the Seahawks. The Raiders went into the season determined to give Mendoza as much time as possible to learn from Cousins and their 4-5 start made it possible to stick with the plan rather than turn attention to the future.

The move would have waited a little while longer if the Vikings were not motivated buyers in the wake of Monday night's disastrous performance against the Bills, but General Manager John Spytek said at a Tuesday press conference that the trade would not have happened without Mendoza showing the team that he's ready.

"It's something that he's worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building," Spytek said. "He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he's earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback."

While the Raiders feel Mendoza is ready, it is a big change to go from the practice field to game action and the Seahawks are a tough first opponent for the rookie. The Raiders drafted Mendoza to be their leader, however, and head coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza has "exceeded those expectations" while learning from a good teacher.

"I think with the right role model that will accelerate his growth and we had, you know, we had the right role model," Kubiak said.

Becoming the starter is just the beginning for Mendoza and it kicks off an era the Raiders hope will bring them back to the upper rungs of the AFC in the years to come.

Peterson's rookie year got off to a slow start in terms of scoring consistency, but he hasn't looked back since notching a then-career-high 21 points two games ago, with follow-up acts of 26 and 25.

He has scored 50% of his field goals or better in each of those games, seasoning the dish with 44% three-point shooting and 4 assists. Peterson has also posted at least one steal in eight of his last nine appearances.

But DP isn't the only young Jazzman bringing defensive effort back to the forefront in SLC; Ace Bailey has been heartless on the defensive end, a constant disruptor whose Plastic Man arms can constantly be seen swinging at shot attempts and deflecting passes.

Better yet, Bailey already has a signature move in just his sophomore season: the 10-foot dribble pull-up.

He picked Miami's defense apart from that sweet spot, but also found comfort behind the three-point line. He had been ice cold in his last six outings. After going 5-for-34 (14.7%) in that stretch, he quenched his three-point thirst with a 3-for-5 outing, 10-for-15 from the field overall.

But Utah's late fourth-quarter burst was jump-started by the most unlikely source: Isaiah Collier's long-range heat checks. Collier went a perfect 4-for-4 from distance and delivered the scoring punch his team needed in a critical moment.

"You saw Zay's reaction," Coach Hardy shared during the post-game presser. "You can see the emotion that Zay plays with and shows, and how much it means to him. Zay has had some things not go his way personally lately, [but] he's been an incredible teammate, he's worked really hard, he's not had one moment of complaining."

In a stretch like this, the Utah Jazz are forced to measure progress in ways that go deeper than the final score, and Collier's timely step-up was massive in igniting that final spark of hope for his teammates.

The Jazz will look to double their win total tomorrow against the Orlando Magic.

Calvin Barrett is the Associate Editor for SLC Dunk and a Utah Jazz columnist for the Standard-Examiner. Originally from Springville, Utah, he currently writes from his desk in Japan.

#2697. Stampede Blue Reacts Survey (Week 10): Are Colts fans confident after major roster changes?

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, where Colts fans and NFL fans nationwide share their opinions throughout the season.

The Indianapolis Colts have officially entered a new chapter following one of the most eventful trade deadlines in franchise history. After parting ways with Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner two weeks ago, Indianapolis continued its roster overhaul Tuesday by sending veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers and Josh Downs to the Kansas City Chiefs. The departures of four established players have allowed the Colts to accumulate additional draft capital, although they have also created significant holes across a roster that was already struggling to compete. With Chris Ballard no longer in charge and a new general manager expected to take over during the offseason, the organization appears increasingly focused on building toward the future rather than salvaging the remainder of 2026.

Interestingly, Jonathan Taylor was one of the few major names who ultimately remained in Indianapolis despite considerable interest from around the league. The Colts reportedly received multiple offers involving second-round selections but maintained a much higher asking price for their star running back, deciding to retain him rather than accept compensation they considered insufficient. Keeping Taylor provides some stability for an offense that has already lost several important contributors, although questions remain about whether his remaining prime seasons will align with the franchise's next competitive window. The decision also leaves the next general manager with an important choice regarding the long-term direction of the offense.

Meanwhile, the situation on the field hasn't improved much. Indianapolis suffered its fifth consecutive defeat Sunday, falling 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys and dropping to 2-7 on the season. Last week's Reacts survey showed that just 19 percent of Colts fans believed the franchise was headed in the right direction, down from 31 percent the previous week and 47 percent two weeks earlier. While the continued losing has understandably frustrated fans, the organization's willingness to make significant changes could provide some optimism that a more sustainable future is being built. With several additional draft selections now available but plenty of uncertainty surrounding the roster, coaching staff and quarterback position, the question remains whether fans believe the Colts are finally taking the necessary steps toward returning to contention.

#2696. Will the Rams regret not making any moves at the trade deadline?

The Los Angeles Rams went all-in this offseason. Now, they're doing it again – only this time with their own guys.

Rather than bringing in some outside help at wide receiver, kicker or punt returner, the Rams are trusting the roster they built over the course of months by standing pat at the trade deadline. They didn't make a single move, passing on the opportunity to add someone like Josh Downs or Keenan Allen, both of whom were moved by the Colts.

The question is, will they regret this gamble?

It's hard to say because the Rams found themselves in a weird limbo state. On the one hand, they're more than talented enough to win the Super Bowl. On the other, they're so banged up and the loss of Puka Nacua for even four games might be too much to overcome on their path to the playoffs.

The Rams offense has been underwhelming all year with Nacua. It's scary to think about what it will look like without him catching 14 passes and seeing nearly half of Matthew Stafford's targets like he did on Sunday against the Commanders.

I mean, the Rams had 343 yards in that game, and Nacua had 170 of them. After his 150 receiving yards, the next-closest player had 20. T-W-E-N-T-Y.

No one is denying that the Rams could've used a wide receiver. Even a veteran past his prime like Allen would've been a big lift. And Downs could've helped on punt returns, too. But there would've been a cost to acquiring one of those players.

Downs cost the Chiefs a fourth- and fifth-rounder, with a seventh-rounder going back to Kansas City. Allen cost the 49ers a sixth-rounder.

Those weren't astronomical prices to pay, but for a team like the Rams that currently has just four picks in the 2027 draft and is missing its second-rounder in 2028, they were limited with the assets they could afford to trade away. Had the Rams traded their fourth- and fifth-round picks for Downs like the Chiefs did, they would've been left with one pick in the first four rounds of next year's draft (pending compensatory picks).

And for a team that will need to rebuild its roster with young talent, it can be hard to part with valuable draft picks – especially considering how often the Rams hit on mid-to-late-rounders.

There's a chance they'll regret not making a move for a receiver. Or a kicker. Or a reliable, impactful return specialist. But at the same time, it's easy to understand why they didn't. Their road to the playoffs just became a lot tougher, and it was incredibly difficult to begin with because of the quality of their opponents. Now it's just a matter of surviving the next four games (or so) until reinforcements come.

Maybe they think Davante Adams will be back right after the bye, which would be huge. Maybe Terrance Ferguson can return in Week 12, too. If that's the case, the Rams will only have to go one more game with Adams, Nacua and Ferguson all out.

Maybe that's the reason the Rams stood pat and feel confident enough in Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels – as hard as that is to believe, given their lack of involvement this season – to go a few more games as the top receivers.

The defense is more than good enough. Now it's on Sean McVay and the offense to adapt and adjust without some of their top playmakers.

This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Will the Rams regret not making any moves at the trade deadline?

#2694. Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns closing in on Willis Reed’s double-double mark

Karl-Anthony Towns will match a legend's franchise record with another double-double.

The Knicks center scored 21 points with 16 boards during Tuesday's blowout victory over the Bucks, notching his 10th straight double-double — which is one off Willis Reed's mark to start the 1970-71 season.

And just like that campaign for Reed, Towns is racking up the rebounds while defending an NBA championship.

The Knicks face the Cavaliers on Wednesday at MSG, where Towns can tie Reed.

Karl-Anthony Towns, who scored 21 points and grabbed 16 boards, rises up for a rebound during the Knicks' 117-85 blowout win over the Bucks on Nov. 10, 2026 at the Garden. NBAE via Getty Images

"I didn't know that. I just know that this team right now, we're on a good winning streak, we're playing good basketball, and that's the most important thing," Towns said. "That's what the fans really want to hear about."

Towns leads the Eastern Conference in rebounds per game at 13.8.

It's a much better start than last season, when KAT's efficiency dipped as he struggled to adjust to Mike Brown's system.

"It's just another year with this team and just experience and just another year with a better understanding of what Mike wants and what I can do to help his system," Towns said.

Taylor Jenkins said coaching the Knicks "just wasn't meant to be" as he reflected on interviewing for New York's open gig last year.

"It was a great experience. I obviously spent a lot of time with the front office — Leon [Rose] and his group. Not sure how close it was in the end. It just wasn't the opportunity at that time," said Jenkins, who lost to the Knicks on Tuesday as the Bucks head coach.

"Very blessed to be where I am right now. But excited to go through the process of interviewing with the Knicks. Learned a lot. Obviously it was a special year last year for the Knicks. Mike [Brown] did a great job. Learned a lot about this organization, the high standards they had. And obviously the great work that they had done even leading up to last season. So it was a fun process to be a part of. Hopefully I performed well and it just wasn't meant to be."

Jenkins and Brown were considered the front-runners for the Knicks job as Rose's search hit the homestretch.

Jenkins had recently been fired by the Memphis Grizzlies, who played well under his watch but failed to get out of the second round of the playoffs.

The Knicks tried to interview several head coaches under contract, but their requests were rejected by the involved teams.

Jenkins was interviewed once, along with former Timberwolves assistant Micah Nori and South Carolina women's coach Dawn Staley.

Brown was the only candidate called back for a second interview — which, according to sources, happened after he was already picked for the job.

Jenkins was unemployed for a year before accepting the Bucks job.

It became a total rebuild project in Milwaukee after Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to the Heat, leaving Jenkins with a bottom-tier roster and a pitiful 1-10 record.

#2693. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2692. 11 true Super Bowl contenders, and their biggest question

We have reached the midway point of the 2026 NFL season.

And it is time to look at some true Super Bowl contenders.

These are the teams in both the AFC and the NFC that, at least right now, look like true contenders for a title. Could a team not on this list make a run? Absolutely, that is the nature of sports. But right now, these are the 11 teams you could make a case for.

Along with the biggest question they will need to answer over the second half of the season.

Through the first half of the NFL season, the Jacksonville Jaguars have put themselves among the league's elite. They lead the way with a point differential of +108 (the only team above 100) and also lead the NFL in turnover differential. Trevor Lawrence is playing like an MVP candidate, and a defense that was good — Jacksonville currently ranks third in Defensive EPA/Play — added a ton of talent ahead of the NFL's trade deadline.

Biggest question: Can the additions put this team over the top?

Jacksonville looked like Super Bowl contenders ahead of the NFL trade deadline, so it is no surprise that general manager James Gladstone was aggressive in acquiring players like Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux. Can those additions truly propel Jacksonville to the Super Bowl?

While the Jacksonville Jaguars grabbed the headlines this week, the Buffalo Bills kept chugging along. Josh Allen and company went into Minnesota and beat the Vikings on "Monday Night Football," improving to 7-1 on the season and keeping themselves atop the AFC standings.

It is easy to simply say that as long as the Bills have Allen, they have a shot. But with James Cook in the backfield and Keon Coleman emerging as something more in the passing game, Buffalo certainly has the offense to contend.

Biggest question: Can the defense step up?

But the defense remains a big question mark. This group looked good on Monday night, but that came at the expense of what we saw from Carson Wentz. Can Buffalo's defense deliver down the stretch?

Hopefully for Bills fans, Amani Hooker is the answer.

A similar case can be made for the Cincinnati Bengals.

Cincinnati certainly has an offense they can rely upon down the stretch. Joe Burrow is playing at an elite level (he is tied for third in Adjusted Net Yards per Attempt with a mark of 8.0), the duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins put pressure on every defensive secondary they face, and Chase Brown gives Cincinnati a option in the ground game. Right now the Bengals are averaging 0.146 Expected Points Added per Play, behind only the San Francisco 49ers.

Biggest question: Can the defense step up?

Stop me if you have heard this before, but the question in Cincinnati centers on the defense.

While this group got out to a decent start, including holding Houston to just six points in a Week 2 win, giving up 36 points to Tennessee two weeks ago is a concerning data point.

The Denver Broncos are a fascinating team.

Looking at Denver through an EPA lens, you see a team that is more "league average" than Super Bowl contender. Denver's talented defense is actually a below-average unit against the pass (when examining EPA/dropback) and the offense is right in the middle of the pack:

And yet there they are at 7-2, at the top of the AFC standings behind only Buffalo. And Denver has two impressive wins on the resume, home victories against both Jacksonville and Kansas City.

While a game against Buffalo on Christmas Day looms large, at the moment they look like contenders.

This is the biggest question, right? Is Bo Nix the quarterback Broncos fans believe he is?

If so, this team can make a deep run. If not …

Patrick Mahomes is back and healthy, at least relatively speaking. Most years that would be enough to mark the Kansas City Chiefs down as Super Bowl contenders. But Kansas City also has stepped up their rushing offense, thanks in large part to the acquisition of Kenneth Walker III last spring, and if you look at the above graphic highlighting offensive efficiency, you'll find the Chiefs among the league's best run games.

But yet, something does feel like it is missing with Kansas City this year.

Biggest question: Where will the explosive plays come from?

While the Chiefs have one of the most explosive run games in the league — Kansas City has seven runs of 20 yards or more, ranking them fifth in the NFL — they have just 22 such passing plays, putting them near the bottom of the league. Can they find explosives in the passing game down the stretch?

Another fascinating team? The Pittsburgh Steelers.

If this were the 1970s, you might consider the Steelers at the top of lists like this one. Pittsburgh has an impressive running game (the Steelers lead the NFL with EPA/rush of 0.097, one of just two teams with a positive number in that category) and a defense that is among the best in the league. The Steelers are sixth in the NFL in EPA/play on defense, and fifth in the league in scoring defense.

But the passing game, that is another story. And since we are not in the 1970s …

Biggest question: Can they get enough from the passing game?

Again, looking at EPA/dropback, the Steelers have some questions to answer in the passing game. Pittsburgh averages -0.069 Expected Points Added per dropback, the seventh-lowest mark in the league.

The San Francisco 49ers just keep chugging along.

Despite an injured list that is as long as the NFL offseason, the 49ers remain at the top of the NFC standings and show no signs of slowing down. San Francisco's Week 8 blip against the Atlanta Falcons aside, the 49ers have the inside track to a division title, and their eyes squarely set on the top spot in the NFC.

Biggest question: What makes this San Francisco team different?

We have seen this before from San Francisco. A team that wins 12 or more games in the regular season, but falls short in the playoffs. Is there something that will make it different this year? Another year of Brock Purdy? The rest of the conference facing even bigger questions? What will be the difference for San Francisco in 2026?

Maybe the return of Brandon Aiyuk will help …

If the NFL playoffs began today, the Chicago Bears would be in as the winners of the NFC North, and one of four teams from the division in the dance.

The reasons to believe in the Bears start on the offensive side of the ball. Caleb Williams has put himself in the MVP mix, and while the four interceptions Monday night against Tampa Bay dealt a blow to those chances, he gives the Bears a way to win every Sunday. And in Ben Johnson's hands, this offense is a problem for most defenses.

Biggest question: Is Jeffery Simmons exactly what the Bears needed?

The questions in Chicago the past few months have focused on the defense. But with the trade for Jeffery Simmons, this group has taken a big step forward. Simmons paid immediate dividends against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 8, and if the defense continues to improve around him down the stretch, this could be a very tough team to beat.

As far as offenses go, the Detroit Lions check a lot of boxes. Jared Goff sits fifth in ANY/A among qualified passers, Jahmyr Gibbs is one of the most explosive players in the league, and looking at EPA, the Lions offense is right where you want to be: Above league average in both EPA/dropback and EPA/rushing attempt.

The question in Detroit, like we have seen with some other teams, comes on the defensive side of the football. The Lions have struggled on defense this season, but that unit is trending in the right direction. The Lions have won four straight games, with the defense holding opponents to under 17 points in each of the last three wins. That includes holding Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers to just 17 points back in Week 7. And with Brian Branch expected to return soon, this defense could be getting better at just the right time.

Biggest question: Has the defense turned a corner?

This is a defense that gave up 30 points to the New Orleans Saints in Week 1, 41 points to the Buffalo Bills in Week 2, 24 points to the New York Jets — THE JETS — in Week 3 and 32 points to the Carolina Panthers in Week 4.

There is a strong case to be made that Jordan Love is the midseason MVP.

In fact, our own Jarrett Bailey made that case on Tuesday.

Yet, something else could help this team down the stretch, and that is the impending return of Micah Parsons. The pass rusher returned to practice last week, and if he is available over the rest of the season, that could turn what has been a average defense into much, much better to close out the year.

Biggest question: What about the offensive line?

We thought Green Bay fixed the offensive line a few weeks ago, but that unit has struggled the past few weeks. Can Matt LaFleur and company find the right combination for the stretch run?

The Vikings actually fell off this list Tuesday morning.

But they were back on it Tuesday afternoon.

Why? The trade for Kirk Cousins. Suddenly an offense that looked awful looked, at least on paper, less so. Will it be enough to save the season in Minnesota?

With the defense Brian Flores is running out there, it just might be.

Biggest question: Is Kirk Cousins the answer?

There is a strong case to be made that Carson Wentz's performance against the Buffalo Bills on Monday night was the worst outing by a Vikings quarterback in franchise history.

If Cousins is just league average down the stretch — or even just slightly below average — that could be enough for Minnesota.

#2691. Utah Jazz vs Miami Heat: Player Grades

I know as well as anyone that the Jazz are currently on a 9 game losing streak. I also know quite well that moral victories do not make their way onto the win column. However, I do not think it is necessarily wrong to adjust our expectations as the season makes known the true quality of the team and players that we are working with. So, in a game with 4 injured starters against a full strength Miami Heat, finding miniature successes beyond the tracked win or loss is likely our best bet to both (a) prevent a full collapse into despair and (b) track where our players currently are, even if they are not where we wish they would be. It was ugly at points, but most of the Jazzmen showed some flash that could theoretically be translated into winning basketball when the stars are aligned and the injury-bug is vanquished.

Note: These grades are more-or-less relative to the player. An A grade for Darryn Peterson is different than an A grade for Tony Bradley.

Scientists are still working out the fine details, but the current consensus is clear; Ace Bailey is physically incapable of missing his signature stop-on-a-dime short midrange jump shot. For the first time in what feels like forever, his range extended beyond his sweet spot – despite a poor three point shooting season overall, Ace went 3 for 5 from downtown tonight. His defense left a little bit to be desired, as he was guarding up the lineup and was sometimes physically outmatched in the paint. Additionally, even though his short midrange is near automatic at this point, his lack of free throw attempts become more and more distressing with each passing game – his 0.7 free throw attempts per game average will not be boosted by his game tonight. He was active and efficient, but the areas of improvement for Ace remain clear.

Mo stuffed the stat sheet in his 17 minutes – 7 points, 7 rebounds, and 3 blocks is nothing to scoff at. However, it was obvious that Giannis was licking his chops whenever he saw Bamba attempting to guard him out on the perimeter – Mo gave Giannis all the space in the world, which isn't necessarily a bad idea, but when Giannis hits 3 jump shots in a row, the time to adjust has arrived. However, it seemed that he simply didn't have the athletic capabilities to throw any other look at the Greek Freak, which sparked the Heat's run in the third quarter. He still brought value by being a large human located in the paint, but Giannis was clearly not an ideal matchup for him.

Worse counting stats than Bamba, but the eye test tells me that his impact was a little bit greater. His one block from this game was shocking to someone who remembers how out of shape Bradley was when he first entered the league – he rotated from the other side of the paint to swat Bam Adebayo with a mobility that a Jazz fan from 2018 would relish. Consistently, he seemed to be in the right place at the right time, which matters a lot when he is also consistently the player with the most mass on the court. The other Jazz center options are long and springy but without the size to really hold up in certain matchups, so Bradley operated as a nice change of pace against the burliness of the Heat frontcourt. This isn't advocating for Bradley to be given more consistent minutes, but he certainly made the most of them tonight.

I originally wrote that this was a tale of two halves for Isaiah Collier, but that doesn't accurately reflect how rapidly his grade rose as the game progressed – really, a better description would be that this was a tale of 3.5 quarters and 1 miraculous end-of-game revival. Throughout most of the game, Collier was actively and obviously detrimental; the Heat weren't respecting his three pointer, he wasn't able to get to the paint consistently to aid the offense through kickouts, and the decision making was jarringly off. However, one of the only moments of real electricity in the Delta Center occurred when Collier drained 4 threes in the 4th quarter and single-handedly dragged the Jazz back into the ball game. He didn't impact the game in a very sustainable way, to be sure; I'm not sure if he'll ever again have a three point shooting game this good in his career, and his bread-and-butter value adds (passing, paint pressure) just weren't clicking. However, sustainable or not, going 4/4 from three in the fourth quarter made this contest competitive and ignited an otherwise stagnant Jazz offense.

Filipowski snags a solid grade simply for not making very many mistakes. His presence was not always actively felt, to be sure, but if you watched him with any intentionality you could tell that the team functioned just a bit better with him on the court. He makes quick decisions, he has the ability (or at least the semblance of it) to dribble+pass+shoot, and he brings one of the better combinations of strength and mobility on the roster. I'm not sure what the tracking data says, but it appeared to me that Filipowski was the Jazz's best matchup against Giannis, where his size and speed clearly didn't rival Miami's star but was enough to at least act as a roadblock on his path to 30 points and 11 rebounds.

The shooting was rough (I recall both an airball and a backboard hit from his corner three attempts) and you still don't ever want him to dribble the ball, but Green consistently brings positive value in just about every other area of the game. His passing was solid (the bounce pass to the cutting Ace Bailey before his reverse jam in the fourth quarter was a highlight) and the rebounding always seemed to come in a timely manner, putting a stop to seemingly never-ending Miami offensive possessions. On top of all this, you can always count on the defense. However, there's only so much value you're actually bringing when you shoot an ugly 1-5 on a team that needed an offensive spark, and that puts a ceiling on Green's grade.

By my eyes, Hayes was clearly the worst of the three Jazz big men who got any run against the Heat. He was physically overmatched going against Giannis and Bam, which created a snowball effect of fouls to frustration to more fouls. Hayes is the big man who I believe is most benefitted by playing with capable offensive players – he doesn't have the strength or ball skills to make anything happen on his own, but his athleticism becomes exponentially more valuable when he has stars to take some of the gravity off of him. Tonight, with 3 key scorers out of commission, you could tell that Hayes was floundering in his search for what he was supposed to provide. On the plus side – I've been relatively impressed with his top-of-the-key playmaking recently: he had a few nice passes to Darryn throughout.

One of the benefits that Svi had last year over his shooting guard peers was that he was one of the few who seemed to try at all defensively. He was never good, mind you, but he was big enough and had enough experience around the NBA to barely surpass some of the guys he was competing against for minutes. This year, however, that is no longer the case. Josh Green and Josh Okogie have made a living off of the defensive end, and Darryn Peterson is also a natural two with higher highs on defense than Svi could ever reach. So, when Svi isn't making his shots, he no longer has the safety net of yesteryear that says "well, he's better than the alternative". I understand that shooters have a short memory, but maybe Svi's could be broadened just a bit, because some of these attempts are really only permissible in the context of a heat check. For Svi's sake, something has got to change, because I currently see him on the fast track to being an international league star, as opposed to someone with a legitimate future in the NBA.

Much of what I wrote for Josh Green could be copy-and-pasted over to fellow Josh, Okogie…except this time the shooting was slightly worse and his decision-making was a bit less snappy. I liked Okogie's defensive effort a bit more in this game than Green's (his tie-up on Antetokounmpo in transition should've been a jump ball), but it wasn't enough to either (a) prevent Giannis, one of his main matchups, from getting to his spots or (b) prevent his +/- from being by far the worst on the team, with a -22. We all know, at this point, what we're getting from Okogie, and his game-to-game value is mostly determined by the dice roll that is his shooting variance. Today, with poor shooting and no star combo guard for him to pester defensively, Okogie was not particularly valuable.

In terms of how much excitement Peterson drummed up within me, this grade would be an easy A+. His poise in the pick-and-roll was immaculate, his touch was impressive from all over the court, and his passing looks slightly ahead of the schedule implied by the Kansas tape. For large swaths of his game, he was the offense: he brought the ball up the court, and the remainder of the shot clock was spent trying to free him up with screens and handoffs. Most impressively to me, he functioned with comfort against the hounding, disruptive nature of Davion Mitchell – on paper, this was an easy matchup to predict giving Peterson loads of trouble, but he still always felt like he had control over his offensive attack, even in spite of the 5 turnovers. However, purely in terms of his output on the court tonight, he was still a few steps away from perfect. He fouled out in the 4th quarter on a pretty ticky-tack call, but a good percentage of his penalties were legitimate and foolishly committed. Additionally, his defense is still very much the defense of a rookie guard; he has the tools to make big plays, but often falls asleep or misses key rotations. I give him plenty of grace due to the context of this being his first game as the true #1 offensive option on an NBA team, but his missteps tonight prevent him from getting the grade that matches our excitement.

You know what, I haven't given up on Brice Sensabaugh. The prevailing opinion seems to be that he cannot positively impact winning, but I just can't agree with that quite yet. Tonight, his scoring isn't what you would have hoped. Only 5 shots for a team clearly in need of a scoring punch was odd and out of character, and does hurt his grade. However, I think he did provide marginal value in a few other areas. For example, there were a few plays where I was quite impressed with his defense against Miami's wings – he met them near the half court line and used his mass to make life a little difficult. In general, he filled the stat sheet, outside of the points column: 4 rebounds, 4 assists, and a steal in 14 minutes isn't too shabby for the microwave scorer archetype. Of course, I can't give too high of a grade – he isn't quite good enough at anything besides scoring for a non-scoring night to be immensely valuable – but I do think that we need to give Brice a bit more grace and a bit more priority minutes-wise as the season progresses.

Who stood out for you? Which grades would you change? Sound off below!

#2690. Colts Get a Subtle Shot From Josh Downs After His Trade to The Chiefs

All Josh Downs wanted was to get away from the Indianapolis Colts via a trade, and he finally saw that happen on Tuesday,

The Colts sent the wide receiver to the Kansas City Chiefs along with a seventh-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft in exchange for a fourth-rounder and fifth-rounder in 2027.

Shortly after the trade, Downs posted a wordless post on X, formerly Twitter, to sum up what he truly felt after finally getting out of Indianapolis.

The 25-year-old Downs simply searched for the famous GIF of former NBA high-flyer Vince Carter's reaction to his jersey getting retired by the Toronto Raptors and hit send.

Nov 23, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Indianapolis wide receiver Josh Downs (2) runs against the Chiefs in the second quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images

#2689. Could Nwaneri's lack of playing time prompt Arsenal to end Dortmund loan early?

After joining Borussia Dortmund on a season-long loan deal just before the summer transfer window closed, Ethan Nwaneri was initially handed decent playing time and started four consecutive Bundesliga games between Matchdays 3 and 6.

However, the 19-year-old's playing time has decreased significantly as the season progressed, and he has played just 47 minutes across five short cameos in BVB's last six games in all competitions.

The lack of playing time is hardly ideal for Dortmund or Nwaneri himself, but it is arguably an even bigger concern for Arsenal, who sent him out on loan specifically to find regular first-team football.

Nwaneri found himself in a similar situation during the second half of last season, when he was on loan at Olympique Marseille. He made just four starts in 11 appearances and was left on the bench for his final four Ligue 1 games

With the Gunners certainly keen to avoid a repeat of that scenario, they could potentially activate the recall clause reportedly included in their agreement with Dortmund, unless Nwaneri's situation improves in the coming weeks.

German outlet Ruhr Nachrichten previously reported that, should Arsenal wish to exercise the clause, they must make their intentions clear "well before the start of the transfer window". Exactly how far in advance they need to do so, however, is unclear.

#2687. Colts ownership just showed “Find a Way” was not to be taken lightly

The challenge came down from the top. Was it a challenge or an ultimatum? Either way, the marching orders for 2026 were set in training camp by the owner of the Indianapolis Colts, Carlie Irsay-Gordon. The mantra was simple: "Find a Way." The underpinnings were subtle but understood, win or else. After the trade deadline, the Colts are finding themselves on the "else" side of things.

DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson, Keenan Allen, and Josh Downs all wear new uniforms now. Grover Stewart and Jonathan Taylor were on the chopping block too. Let's not forget about Chris Ballard either. David Bowie sang about "changes," and the Colts organization has gone through plenty. The worst or possibly best part of it all is that those changes don't appear to be done.

Irsay-Gordon inherited a mess with a team that hasn't produced in a decade and a GM who was around for all of it. Her message sent a shot across the bow, seemingly, in the softest way possible. Find a Way was all she said. What she meant can be seen from top to bottom in this organization. Shane Steichen and Daniel Jones' days appear to be numbered too. The production isn't there, and they haven't found a way, to say the least.

New owners, coaches, or even CEOs of companies like to have their own people, those that fit their vision. The good ones don't come in and start slashing without cause, though. If someone shows their worth and circumstances are right, chances are they stay. Irsay-Gordon did that. Everyone got another chance. She could have cleaned house when she took over. She would have been more than justified to do that after last year's collapse too, but she didn't. Everyone got plenty of grace, but the NFL isn't built on grace. It is built on winning. It is built on finding a way to win no matter what.

Pieces of this once-proud franchise are scattered on the ground. The facade is broken and all is exposed. When put under the microscope and intense pressure to perform, the Colts couldn't. If they can't do it, Carlie Irsay-Gordon will find someone who can because that's what it's about. Win, just win. Find a way to fight through it, make the play, and come out on top. Right now, the Colts are at the bottom. It's going to take a lot, but this organization must find a way to rise, once again, to the top.

#2686. Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?

EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon's plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night.

Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said.

"He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team," Lanning said. "Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He's gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it'll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do.

"He's also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we've done."

Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks' offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois.

Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go.

"They see the football coach, right? That's also an unbelievable dad. A great husband," Lanning said. "The guy's been part of our staff for the last five years, that's done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. Because we didn't create success for our team this season."

#2685. Game Preview: San Antonio Spurs at Chicago Bulls

It feels as though the Chicago Bulls will never escape the cycle of mediocrity that has largely affected the franchise since Michael Jordan's retirement all the way back in 1998. After the latest handful of meandering seasons, Chicago made the decision last February at the trade deadline to trade or move on from a handful of their better players and go all-in on yet another rebuilding expedition. Between the struggles that are expected to come with any rebuilding roster and a brutal schedule to kick off this year that has seen them play the Boston Celtics, New York Knicks, and Philadelphia 76ers two times each already, first year head coach and former championship player with the Spurs Tiago Splitter's group has limped out to a putrid 1-8 start, with very little relief in sight.

They're welcoming in a San Antonio Spurs team tonight that's been firing on all cylinders and is looking for their 10th straight win. While some of the competition has been nothing worth bragging about, San Antonio has been taking care of their business and more or less smashing the opposition. With Victor Wembanyama looking like the apex predator on both ends of the floor that he was destined to become and a supporting group that's growing along with him, the Spurs are right where they want to be.

San Antonio Spurs (9-2) at Chicago Bulls (1-8)November 11 2026 | 7:00 PM CTWatch: DAZN | Listen: WOAI (1200 AM)Line: Spurs -14.5

Spurs Injuries: Tobias Harris, calf (OUT), Devin Vassell, groin (questionable)

Bulls Injuries: Norman Powell, shoulder (questionable), Tobe Awaka, back (questionable), Zach Collins, illness (questionable)

It's no secret that Victor Wembanyama has been on a tear since his 1/13 clinker to kick off the season. That performance feels like a lifetime ago, especially in light of two of his most recent games, performances that put him in the same category with two of the greatest big men to ever play the game including San Antonio's own, the Admiral David Robinson. With Chicago boasting arguably the league's worst interior defense, there should be no reason at all not to expect Wembanyama to impose his will on Chicago the way he's done to everyone else this season. Pay attention to how comfortable Wembanyama has become as the roll man out of the pick and roll.

The Bulls' offense is going to have their hands full trying to score against this San Antonio defense. The Spurs have been among the elite in terms of defense this year, ranking 4th in defensive rating with a mark of 107.4 points per 100 possessions thanks to Wembanyama and the intensity and activity of wing players like Stephon Castle and Devin Vassell. The Bulls do push the ball early and often, as is explemplified by their first place ranking in pace, but without any consistent play finishers it hasn't really mattered. Barring a San Antonio no-show, the Silver and Black's defense should be able to hold Chicago down once again.

Games like this always bring to mind Gregg Popovich's, "appropriate fear," mantra. As rough as Chicago has looked this season, there's always the fear of the dreaded trap game. A potential 10-game win streak and 6-0 road record to start the season coming to a halt by a league bottom-dweller feels like the sort of sick irony that die-hard sports fans lose sleep over, but this is still the NBA and anything could happen. Mitch Johnson's group has looked and played pretty determined though during this current streak and have taken care of business against more than one bad team, so it's easy to see them coming into the Windy City and holding up their end of the bargain.

#2683. The NFL’s 6 biggest disappointments so far

Every year it feels like we hit the midpoint of the NFL season and say, "This is the wildest season we've seen." Football has been blessed with incredible parity in recent years, leading to a scenario where the league can fully embrace the idea that anything can happen from week to week. This means stunning breakout performances, and also crushing disappointments.

It's those disappointments we're focusing on today. Events that shattered our previously held beliefs going into the 2027 season and now helping shape the narrative of this year in football. In truth, a lot of these probably come as shocks to the teams as well, with organizations scrambling to find answers before it's too late. When the dust settles on the season these are the elements we're likely to look back on and say that they defined the season.

Sitting at 5-4 the Rams are a middling football team. Nothing more, nothing less. What makes this so mind-boggling is how confident we all were that Sean McVay's team would be a dominant force in football. Sure, we can point to Myles Garrett being hurt for the bulk of the first half of the season, but that doesn't explain how we reach Week 9 and Los Angeles can only beat the hapless Commanders by one-score.

Everything got off on the wrong foot with McVay having a horrific miscalculation on how to approach the season opener in Australia against the 49ers. Now it's as if the Rams have never really shaken that rust off. Matthew Stafford has taken a significant step back after an MVP-winning 2026 season. He has thrown nine interceptions already, on pace for 17 — which would be his highest total since the 2021 season. While slated to throw for 30 touchdowns this year, which would be 16 fewer than a year ago. We didn't expect Stafford to match his 2026 totals, but there's been a pronounced drop-off which has damaged the Rams' offense.

Moreover, on the other side of the ball we were hyped for Los Angeles before the Myles Garrett addition because Trent McDuffie was such a fantastic addition to the secondary. McDuffie has been individually brilliant, but there hasn't been much of a trickle-down effect on the rest of the defense. The Rams are only fractionally better in scoring defense than they were with a no-name secondary a year ago, allowing 20.1 points per game to 20.4 in 2026.

Los Angeles is just woefully inconsistent. One week they will beat the Bills, the next they'll lose to the Cardinals. All while playing one of the softest schedules in the NFL right now. Now they'll need to fight in the back-half of the season to find a wild card spot, so long as San Francisco keeps winning.

Staying in Los Angeles we can single out the most disappointing player of the year in Justin Herbert. It goes without saying that the 0-8 Chargers are the worst team in the NFL, but inside that we also have the most confusing regression we've ever seen from a quarterback, for seemingly no reason.

The core traits Herbert has displayed since entering the league in 2020 were his processing, decision-making, and ability to take care of the football. Until 2026, he threw a total of 58 interceptions in his career, averaging 9.6 per season. It's week nine, and Herbert is already at 11 interceptions and on pace for 24 — which would be more than 2023, 2024, and 2025 combined. These aren't 50/50 picks either, Herbert is making horrible reads, sailing the ball on deep passes into the arms of opponents, and just failing to read the defense all together.

It's impossible to understand what has gone wrong, because it all feels so nonsensical. We could postulate that Herbert hasn't been comfortable in the Mike McDaniel offense, or that he's being asked to throw his way back into games far too often — but even those explanations don't fully explain what has happened. One of the reasons the McDaniel hire looked like such a home run for Herbert and the Chargers is that he only ever asked Tua Tagovailoa to take care of the football, then schemed ways to get players open and take advantage of their accuracy. The same should have worked perfectly with Herbert, but instead he morphed into a pumpkin before Halloween.

Unquestionably the most disappointing single season from a player so far.

The Colts are in the midst of selling off their best players following a 2-7 start to the season. Head coach Shane Steichen will be gone after this year, and the team will be left as a hollow shell needing to be rebuilt — but without a 1st round draft pick, which is owed to the Jets as part of their trade for Sauce Gardner a year ago.

Indianapolis was one of the biggest surprises in the NFL this time last year. In the second week of November they were sitting at 8-2, seemed destined to win the AFC South, and everything was coming up roses. Instead it's turned into an abject disaster, with none of the team's moves paying off, Daniel Jones struggling, Sauce Gardner being one of the worst trades in recent memory, and everything falling apart. The only decent thing the Colts have is Jonathan Taylor, who could well be traded ahead of the deadline.

One move which isn't being discussed enough was the Colts decision to let Michael Pittman Jr. walk in order to re-sign Alec Pierce to a huge contract. Indianapolis liked Pierce's big play ability, and felt they could easily replace Pittman.

Pierce has been injured for much of the year, but even before that he was playing mediocre football. It's not like Pittman has exploded for the Steelers, but it's appearing as if the decision to pay Pierce big money is coming back to bite them.

This team went from one that should have been contending in the AFC South, to now being one of the worst teams in all of football.

I'm on the record for being extremely bullish on the Vikings this year, saying before the season began that they were being slept on more than any other team in the league. Minnesota is now sitting at 6-2 on the season, having only lost to two elite teams in Detroit and Buffalo — even then the only reason they struggled was because of bad quarterback play.

There was a time it seemed that adding Kyler Murray under center would be the injection this offense desperately needed, but that just hasn't happened. Murray is playing scared, ineffective football — which has reached a point where he can't do the one thing he was brought to Minnesota to achieve: Get Justin Jefferson the ball.

The Vikings have massive issues at quarterback because none of their bets have paid off. Murray is extremely disappointing, feeling like a high-tier backup than a former No. 1 pick at this point in his career. Meanwhile the decision to trade away J.J. McCarthy may have backfired as well, while he's surging ahead with the Giants. This makes Murray a double-dose of disappointment where he's played poorly, and he's hurt the team structure because of the belief they placed in him.

Can the Texans please just find some dang consistency? We saw last season as one of the league's best defenses was let down in the playoffs due to C.J. Stroud. Now the offense is playing phenomenally well, and the defense (which has really had no changes) is playing like garbage.

In every single area the Texans have taken a step back from 2025.

18th in total yards allowed (1st in 2025)

There's just no consistency as every single player on defense has let this team down. Will Anderson and Azeez Al-Shaair are the only players upholding their ends of the bargain, and everyone else has been mediocre. Derek Stingley Jr. is allowing a 95.5 passer rating against this season, a staggering falloff from a year ago — and now it's as if the Texans offense needs to win by shootouts because of their struggles.

The Eagles just suck. No way to sugarcoat it. While it's true that Jalen Hurts' injury really threw a wrench in things, the Eagles were mediocre before that happened. This was a team supposed to cruise to an easy NFC East championship, maybe have to contend with the Cowboys — and that was really it.

Instead, they stepped on rakes for so long it busted their face, leaving them utterly incapable of playing effectively this season. Rotten from the top down, the only question remaining is whether or not Philadelphia has the guts to make some of the difficult choices needed in the offseason to get this team back on the right track.

#2681. YouTube Gold: Havlicek Stole The Ball!

John Havlicek is one of the greatest and most unusual players in NBA history, and also one of the most underrated.

That sounds like a contradiction, but it's not. People truly don't understand who great he was, and that includes a lot of the people who saw him play.

We don't know if anyone ever really studied Havlicek's physiology, but it was crazy. In this video, former teammate Sam Jones said that not only did Havlicek never get tired, he didn't even start sweating for 10 minutes. This is in the NBA, against teams filled with great athletes, and of course, Boston was a fast-breaking team. Add guts and brilliant instincts to the mix, and you have Havlicek.

His energy level and endurance probably played a role in his most memorable play. At the end of Game 7 of the 1965 Eastern Conference Finals, Bill Russell tried to inbounds the ball, but it hit a guy wire connected to the backboard.

Philadelphia called a timeout, and Russell pleaded with his teammates to bail him out.

Havlicek obliged, making one of the three most iconic steals in Celtics history, and preserving the win for the Celtics.

The other two: Gerald Henderson's against Los Angeles in the 1984 Finals, and Larry Bird's against Detroit in 1987.

This is the best video/explanation we've seen about Havlicek's enduring moment of glory.

#2680. Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'

EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday.

"There was an incident this weekend that didn't match our standard here in our program," Lanning said. "There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I'm not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We're gonna handle that with our guys.

"There's an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I'm not going to speak on it publicly."

When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven't been any confirmed arrests, he said, "I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it."

This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra'Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27.

An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn't been set, as official charges haven't been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records.

Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday's win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury.

Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday.

#2678. Lions scouting report: Patriots’ strengths, weaknesses

For the first time since 2015, the Detroit Lions are heading overseas! The Lions have played only two international games in their history—going 1-1 in London, England—but this time they're headed to Munich, Germany. Entering this matchup, they've won four straight games and want to keep that streak alive while claiming their first-ever win in Germany.

Detroit takes on the New England Patriots, who appear to be in a rough spot right now, losing two of their last three games and barely above .500. Coming off a Super Bowl appearance last season, New England is currently the seven seed in the AFC, and with injuries also piling up, they've got a lot to overcome to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Let's take a deep look at the Patriots' season so far as they head into Week 10.

Week 1: Lost to Seattle Seahawks 13-10Week 2: Defeated Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3Week 3: Lost to Jacksonville Jaguars 35-6Week 4: Defeated Buffalo Bills 29-26Week 5: Defeated Las Vegas Raiders 45-17Week 6: Defeated New York Jets 26-19Week 7: Lost to Chicago Bears 30-24Week 8: Defeated Miami Dolphins 24-19Week 9: Lost to Green Bay Packers 45-27

Quarterback Drake Maye has had a rocky performance after being an MVP finalist last season. He had a rough first month, throwing "meatball subs," as the kids say nowadays. Maye played well but had an abysmal Week 9, throwing three interceptions. This season, Maye is averaging 253.6 yards per game with 18 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, tied for the league lead in interceptions.

The Patriots' running game has been lackluster this season. Second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson is in a sophomore slump, compounded by injuries, with just 203 yards, a touchdown, and 3.9 yards per carry. Starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson hasn't been explosive either, averaging 3.9 yards per carry with 399 yards and two touchdowns—and he could be held out of this game with a knee tendon issue. The team has seen a little bit of life in third-string back Corey Kiner, who is averaging 4.9 yards per carry with 244 yards and a touchdown.

At receiver, it's been an interesting ride: the Patriots traded for wide receiver A.J. Brown to be their top receiver after losing Stefon Diggs in free agency, and Brown has battled ankle injuries, playing in only three games with 101 yards on nine catches. The top receiver currently is DeMario Douglas, who leads the team in yards (434) and touchdowns (four). The Patriots also signed Romeo Doubs in free agency to a big contract, and he is currently on IR, though he will return this season—he's got 261 yards and three touchdowns in 2026.

One reason for the running game struggles is injuries on the offensive line. The Patriots are without both starting guards, Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker, and now left guard Ben Brown will most likely miss this week's game, according to head coach Mike Vrabel. PFF ranks them 19th in run blocking (62.7), which plays a big part in why the running backs can't find success on the ground. With them not having success on the ground, that puts more pressure on Maye to air it out, and suddenly he's turnover-happy, trying to make plays for the offense.

On defense, the front seven has done a solid job overall. EDGE Elijah Ponder leads the team with 7.5 sacks and is tied for fourth-most in the NFL. Defensive tackle Christian Barmore has 4.5 sacks while rookie EDGE Gabe Jacas has 3.0.

The secondary has been about average, as newly extended cornerback Christian Gonzalez has six pass deflections and a 51.4 PFF coverage grade. Former Lions cornerback Carlton Davis III has been doing well, with a 72 coverage grade. Nickelback Marcus Jones has played well, tied with Gonzalez for the team-leading six pass deflections, and earned a 59.5 coverage grade.

New England is allowing a 67.5 percent completion percentage, the third-highest in the NFL, and is just nine yards behind the Lions for most passing yards allowed this season (2,256), according to Next Gen Stats. They've allowed some big plays in the air, including 32 20+ yard passing plays (second-most) and seven 40+ passing-yard plays (tied for fourth-most). Despite the pass rush getting home, it isn't getting there fast enough for the secondary to hold up its end of the bargain. With teams struggling to run against New England, they've had to air it out and risk that pressure, and the secondary has had its share of woes.

Key players ruled out: WR Romeo Doubs (IR), G Mike Onwenu (IR), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (IR), LB Harold Landry III (PUP)Key players to monitor: WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness), LT Will Campbell (knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), CB Carlton Davis III (knee), LG Ben Brown (knee)

Injuries have started to pile up for the Patriots over the past few weeks. It started after Week 1 when A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury and went to IR. He has returned from IR but has played only two games, as the injury is still bothering him. He has missed the last two games and, according to Tom Pelissero, should return sooner rather than later, perhaps after the Week 11 bye.

In his absence, Doubs and Mack Hollins stepped up but also suffered injuries: Hollins just returned from IR in Week 9, while Doubs is set to return from IR after the team's bye week. The interior offensive line has seen both starting guards, Onwenu and Vera-Tucker, land on IR, with Vera-Tucker likely returning this season, though Onwenu's status remains up in the air. New England is still waiting to activate linebacker Harold Landry III off PUP as well.

Week 9 was a bad week for New England injuries, starting with Henderson having a medical emergency that forced him to miss the game; his status is unknown. On the field, the Patriots saw four starters go down, all with knee injuries. Left tackle Will Campbell, Stevenson, Davis III, and Brown all left the game and didn't return with their injuries. Campbell told the media after the game that he's fine, while Vrabel didn't provide an update on Stevenson or Davis III on Monday.

New England's defense has been helping this team a lot, especially in stopping the run and getting to the quarterback. Starting with the pass rush, New England has 25 sacks overall, tied for ninth most in the league. Ponder has been playing lights out and has given this defense a big spark in their pass-rushing abilities. PFF grades them with an 82.8 pass rush grade, second-highest in the NFL.

This front seven can do more than get to the quarterback; they can also slow down the running game. They've allowed an average of 3.9 yards per carry, tied for ninth-fewest. More impressively, though, they've allowed only one run over 20 yards, for 34. This team makes it really hard to run the football and dares you to drop back to throw it.

When you're forced to air it out, that pass rush comes into play and pressures your quarterback. It's a seesaw battle opposing offenses have to deal with. Do you go aggressive and try to run on them, or lean on your passing game to hopefully light it up? If the passing game succeeds, it opens the door for the run game to have a better chance of breaking one through; if you can't do either, it's going to be a long day for your offense.

While the data and numbers show the Patriots offense is average to slightly above average, injuries are piling up on that side of the ball. Maye has barely had his top two wide receivers together, and now possibly both of his top two running backs could be missing time as well. It doesn't help that the team is already down two starting guards, and one of their replacements won't be playing. Campbell has been playing great at left tackle, so if he somehow misses this game, it could really hurt New England's chances at winning.

Maye hasn't been consistent, and it's hard when you don't have all five starters in front of you for protection and your top weapons on the sidelines. New England has leaned on him to help with ground-game struggles, but with Hollins and Douglas as the top receivers, it's tougher to expect much production than with Brown and Doubs. Maye is doing all he can, but he's taken a step back from last season.

These injuries are piling up, and sure, some of the players will return and aren't gone for the year, but if they don't return soon, there might be nothing left to play for when they do. The AFC isn't as dominant as the NFC, so New England can afford a few losses, but you don't have an avalanche to start, and suddenly it's December and fans are waiting for the 2027 NFL Draft in April.

Key matchup: Lions ground attack vs. Patriots front seven

This matchup will likely determine who wins this football game. While Detroit's ground attack hasn't had many big plays yet, the longest being a 30-yard rush, it's still a strong part of who they are as an offense. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is having a solid season and making his case for MVP consideration. Detroit averages 4.4 yards per carry and has found the end zone 10 times on the ground.

I mentioned earlier how the Patriots' run defense has been solid, and this will be a good-on-good battle. Detroit has a plethora of weapons in the passing game, and they can win through quarterback Jared Goff if need be. Against the Packers last week, the Patriots allowed 372 passing yards, and Detroit's strong passing attack could give the Patriots secondary PTSD. While Detroit can lean on the passing game, that doesn't mean it wants to, and it will keep trying to run the ball on this Patriots front seven. If Detroit can break through this unit and move the ball on the ground, that opens the door for the passing game to find success too.

If New England holds its ground and keeps opposing running backs down, Detroit could run into trouble. In their two losses, Gibbs totaled 98 rushing yards and only one touchdown on the ground. Detroit's offense can survive a rough Gibbs game, but we haven't seen them do it so far in 2026. If the Patriots can contain Gibbs, Detroit could have a long flight home.

Vegas line for Sunday: Lions favored by 2.5

#2677. Paul George steals the show in his return to Philadelphia

Going into Tuesday's Celtics-76ers game, the story was Jayson Tatum vs. Jaylen Brown. Then, Paul George stole the show.

In his return to Philadelphia, George lit up his former team with 36 points and 5 rebounds while shooting 14/22 from the field and 6/11 from three.

George talked to NBC's NBA Showtime crew after the game about how comfortable he is in Boston.

"I'm a little bit better with more usage and that's no knock to how my opportunities here with Philly," George said. "Quite frankly, I wasn't healthy to take on the workload that I feel I'm at my best at. Here in Boston, they gave me an opportunity to come out here and play and be myself."

George has talked a lot about how much he's loved Boston and how he feels healthy early in his Celtics tenure.

His play has been better than even the biggest optimists could have expected.

In the marquee matchup, he was getting to his spots and knocking down shots througout the game.

"I thought he was great," head coach Joe Mazzulla said. "That's just what we need. We need him to play two-way basketball and be great. And you kind of saw that there, especially at the start of the fourth quarter."

George has proven to be a huge part of what the Celtics want to do this season on both sides of the floor. His shooting, both from inside and outside the arc, and secondary playmaking have been a big part of the offense. While he didn't have any steals on Tuesday, his deflections and ability to cause turnovers have played a big part of one of the best defenses in the NBA.

He is a huge part of this group and after another monster game in front of a national audience, proved it once again. George has flashed back to his prime in a big way to start off his Celtics tenure and shown he remains a really good player, though C's fans shouldn't be too surprised by this after last season's first round.
